Two payload fields are not carried: `comment` (the inline submission body) and `restrictReasonType` (why a document is withheld). documents.coverage: Sampled repair with retained prior rows. Calendar searches must distinguish source dates from instants. Under the
Regulations.gov convention in SpicyDocs' `regulations_gov_day`, date-only
values and bare `T00:00:00Z` retain their printed day; other offset-bearing
timestamps use `America/New_York`, not their UTC date. For example,
`2026-10-05T03:59:59Z` is October 4 at 23:59:59 EDT, while
`2026-11-24T04:59:59Z` is November 23 at 23:59:59 EST. This bare-midnight
exception is source-specific, not a rule for arbitrary timestamps.

This guarded DuckDB example selects October 2–16 inclusive in Eastern
calendar days (not a 14-day instant interval). It handles the shown ISO
forms, preserving the source's date-only convention; year zero, malformed
values and offset-free timestamps yield NULL. Inspect those unknowns
separately rather than treating exclusion from the filter as no deadline.
Do not compare UTC timestamp strings with a date-only upper bound.

```sql
WITH calendar AS (
  SELECT document_id,
    CASE
      WHEN left(v, 4) = '0000' THEN NULL
      WHEN regexp_full_match(v, '[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}(T00:00:00Z)?')
        THEN TRY_CAST(left(v, 10) AS DATE)
      WHEN regexp_full_match(v, '[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T.+(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})')
        THEN CAST(TRY_CAST(v AS TIMESTAMPTZ) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York' AS DATE)
    END AS end_day
  FROM (SELECT document_id, trim(comment_end_date) AS v FROM documents)
)
SELECT document_id, end_day FROM calendar
WHERE end_day >= DATE '2026-10-02' AND end_day < DATE '2026-10-17';
```

A date field alone does not establish submission purpose or the legally
controlling/current deadline. For example, FR 2026-15634's DATES text
specifies October 2, 2026 objections/hearing requests under 40 CFR part 178,
not ordinary comments. NULL does not establish that no deadline exists.
Read the notice's filing instructions and later notices before acting.
`fr_docket_links` offers source docket navigation; `comment_periods` offers
derived date-window candidates, not a complete legal extension history.

Rows are additive. The Mirrulations mirror keeps every capture and never
sees a deletion, so a posting Regulations.gov later removes, or moves to
another docket, stays here: on 2026-10-03 FNA-2026-0301-0004, the Utah
notice (FR 2026-18893) filed to the Idaho docket, answered 404 while this
table held it with `withdrawn = 'false'`; Regulations.gov had re-posted it
as FNA-2026-0313-0006, and its four comments appear under both. A daily
step lists every docket with a document posted or modified in the past
week and reads by id each held document the listing omits:
`publisher_status` is `removed` where Regulations.gov answers 404 or 410.
Older dockets are not checked, so NULL means never checked, not still
published. Removed rows stay here; `agency_stats`, `feed_summary`,
`agency_monthly_volume` and `discovery_signals` leave them and their
comments out. Filter `publisher_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'removed'` to do
the same.

columns.description: Unique document identifier. Primary key / dedup key.
Parent docket this document belongs to. Foreign key to `dockets.docket_id`.

Posting agency's short code. `lookup_agency` resolves it through RefSpec's REF-038 projection: measured 2026-10-30, 307 of 316 codes on 2,003,671 of 2,004,396 rows; the rest (`USC`, `BSC`, `TRAIN`, `PCSCOTUS`, `GAPFAC`, `ERULE`, `ARCTICGAS`, `PRES`, `EOA`) have no projection row.
Document title.
Document category (e.g. `Rule`, `Proposed Rule`, `Notice`, `Supporting & Related Material`).
Date the document was posted publicly (ISO 8601 string).
Timestamp the document was last modified (ISO 8601 string).
Literal Regulations.gov commentStartDate. See data_quality for the source-specific calendar conversion; this field does not establish submission purpose. NULL means no value was retained.

Literal Regulations.gov commentEndDate as Regulations.gov states it now, which can reflect a later extension rather than the notice's own date: when a later notice extends the period, Regulations.gov can rewrite the original notice's date too (FS-2025-0001-223869, FR 2026-16965, reads 2026-10-07T03:59:59Z, the extension FR 2026-18648 set, while the Register's comments_close_on for 2026-16965 is 2026-09-21). For the date a notice printed, read federal_register.comments_close_on by fr_doc_num. Convert offset-bearing instants to America/New_York for calendar searches; date-only values and the source's bare T00:00:00Z convention keep their printed day (see data_quality). Neither purpose nor the controlling/current deadline follows from this field; inspect filing instructions and later notices. NULL does not mean no deadline.
URL of the document's primary downloadable rendition. Retained for backward compatibility; see `attachments` for the full list. Often null.

columns.column_type: STRUCT(url VARCHAR, format VARCHAR, size BIGINT)[]
columns.description: Native list of the main document's fileFormats renditions: `[{url, format, size}]`. This compatibility field does not contain separately listed attachment resources. Null when no main renditions were retained. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.description: Native list of the main document's fileFormats renditions: `[{url, format, size}]`. This compatibility field does not contain separately listed attachment resources. Null when no main renditions were retained. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
Federal Register document number, when the document was published in the FR. Often null.

Whether regulations.gov flags the posting withdrawn, as the string `"true"`/`"false"`. Often null. A withdrawn posting is still held here; the rulemaking tables read it as no evidence (see `proceedings`).
Agency-supplied reason for withdrawal, when withdrawn: usually that it was posted to the wrong docket, a duplicate, moved or replaced. Often null.

Native list of additional Regulation Identifier Numbers beyond the docket's primary RIN. Often null. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
Plain text extracted from the document's PDF attachment(s) by the PDF text-extraction step. Null until that step has run; see `text_extraction_status`.

Aggregate PDF outcome: `ok` means at least one PDF supplied text, even if another failed; otherwise `error`, `encrypted`, or `empty` (no extractable text) in that order. Null before an attempt. See `pdf_extraction_results_json` for each file.

Ordered JSON array from the latest PDF attempt: `{url, source_sha256, status, page_count, error}` per distinct selected URL. SHA-256 identifies observed bytes; no-bytes fetch failures have null digest/page count and a generic error. Null when no PDF attempt is recorded. Describes that attempt, not the provenance of older text retained after a failed overwrite.

What Regulations.gov last said of the document when the daily reconcile step checked its docket: `listed` (the docket's document listing names it, or, where the listing does not, its own record still answers) or `removed` (the listing omits it and its own record answers 404 or 410). NULL where the step has never checked it: it checks only dockets with a document posted or modified in the past week, so NULL does not mean the publisher still serves it. A removed document stays in this table (see data_quality).
When the reconcile step first found the document removed, as a UTC ISO 8601 instant; NULL unless `publisher_status` is `removed`.

observed_off_list.reason: regulations.gov returns this documentType on 374 document rows and labels it in its own web UI, but the pinned v4 OpenAPI DocumentType enum lists only five values and does not include it. The publisher's documentation is incomplete; the data is not wrong.

comments.label: Public comments
comments.summary: One posted public-comment record, linked to its stated docket and parent document when those references are supplied. Null docket references remain in the table and agency totals. Attachments, source text and extraction results are separate observations; missing text or file URLs do not prove the publisher received no attachment. Agency-partitioned publication supports scoped record queries.
comments.coverage: True range, floored and open-ended. Posted dates are stated from 1990-01-01 rather than from the raw minimum of year 0000, on the same publisher defect as `documents`; the mirror is rebuilt from the catalog, so the latest posted date is a query (`SELECT max(posted_date)`), not a stated bound. See the data-quality note.
comments.data_quality: Rows with a `posted_date` before 1990 carry the same publisher defect as `documents` (`WHERE posted_date < '1990'` counts them); filter on the date when recency matters. A comment on a posting Regulations.gov removed stays here, and where the publisher moved the posting it re-posted the comments under new ids, so one comment can appear twice: on 2026-10-03 FNA-2026-0301-0006 to -0009, on the removed FNA-2026-0301-0004, are FNA-2026-0313-0002 to -0005, body for body. `agency_stats` and `feed_summary` leave them out; to do the same, keep rows `WHERE comment_on_document_id IS NULL OR comment_on_document_id NOT IN (SELECT document_id FROM documents WHERE publisher_status = 'removed')`.

columns.description: Unique comment identifier. Primary key / dedup key.
Source-supplied docket identifier for joining to `dockets.docket_id`. Null when the source does not identify a docket; mirror directory names and comment ID prefixes do not fill this field.

Literal Regulations.gov commentOnDocumentId: the named parent document, independently nullable from docket_id. No identifier-prefix inference. The comment re-read filled it: on receipt sha256:77a08369… (2026-10-03) it is set on 26,388,456 of 26,415,400 rows, on at least 98.97% of each of the 12 largest agencies' rows, and below 95% only at MSHA (1,892 of 1,993) and TRAIN (1 of 114). NULL means the record states none or the row was not read; `comment_reference_values_json` tells the two apart. NULL does not mean the comment names no document.
Literal commentOn in the native object-ID namespace; not interchangeable with a public document key.
Literal originalDocumentId, retained as an unresolved legacy source reference.
JSON map containing only present source parent-reference fields, preserving null and empty values. {} means the source was read and fields were absent; SQL NULL means legacy or unread.
Receiving agency's short code.

Commenter's first name, where the row's read carried it. NULL where the publisher's record states none or where the row's read did not carry the field; `count(first_name)` by `agency_code` is the measure.

Commenter's last name, where the row's read carried it. NULL where the publisher's record states none or where the row's read did not carry the field; `count(last_name)` by `agency_code` is the measure.

The organization the commenter stated, where the row's read carried it. NULL where the publisher's record states none (FDA and EPA state none; EPA classifies submitters in `subtype` instead) and where the row's read did not carry the field. A campaign record carries it where the publisher states it: on receipt sha256:77a08369… (2026-10-03) FWS states it on 340 of its 408 `Mass Mail Campaign` and 10 of its 13 `Late Mass Mail Campaign` records, EPA on none of 7,842. `count(organization)` by `agency_code` is the measure.

Submitter category as regulations.gov states it, where the row's read carried it (FDA's records state one, such as `Individual Consumer` or `Private Industry - C0003`). NULL where the publisher's record states none (EPA states none: it classifies submitters in `subtype` and counts campaigns in `duplicate_comments`) or where the row's read did not carry the field; NULL across a whole agency does not mean the agency does not classify. `count(category)` by `agency_code` is the measure.
Comment title / subject line, as the publisher serves it; a few carry HTML entities (`'`, `&`).

The comment body as regulations.gov serves it: an HTML fragment, not plain text. Line breaks are `
` tags and many characters are HTML entities (`'`, `"`, `&`, `’`) on many rows of every agency, so a pattern with a plain apostrophe or quotation mark misses them: replace the entities before grouping or quoting. Filled for nearly every comment. Text of attached files is in `text_content`, which is filled only where an attachment was extracted. The largest field in the dataset.
Document category for the comment record, typically `Public Submission`.

When the comment was posted, as the publisher stamps it (ISO 8601 string): a date at Eastern midnight written in UTC (`T04:00:00Z` or `T05:00:00Z`) on most records, a bare date label at `T00:00:00Z` on others. Read the date part as the publisher's date; converting a `T00:00:00Z` label to Eastern moves it a day early.
Timestamp the comment was last modified (ISO 8601 string).
The agency's stated receipt date, stamped as `posted_date` is (ISO 8601 string). It can follow `posted_date` (late or mailed submissions), so compare on the date part.

columns.column_type: STRUCT(title VARCHAR, formats STRUCT(url VARCHAR, format VARCHAR, size BIGINT)[], attachment_id VARCHAR, restrict_reason VARCHAR, restrict_reason_type VARCHAR)[]
columns.description: Native ordered list of attachment entries, including restricted attachments and renditions without a URL. `restrict_reason_type` and `restrict_reason` retain the stated restriction. NULL means the included set was absent or unavailable in that row; [] means it contained no attachment entries. A format list or rendition URL can be NULL. Older rows may retain the earlier filtered representation; NULL never proves attachment absence.

Plain text of the comment's attachment(s). Filled inline during the ETL from Mirrulations' own extraction (the bucket's `derived-data` prefix): one extraction tool per comment, its attachments in number order, each stripped and separated by a blank line; when that tool's objects are all blank there is no derived text. Attachments Mirrulations has not extracted are backfilled by the on-demand PDF text-extraction step. Null when neither has produced text; see `text_extraction_status`.

Where `text_content` came from, or why there is none. `derived` means Mirrulations' own extraction supplied it (see `pdf_extraction_results_json`); `ok` means Spicy Regs extracted text from at least one PDF, even if another failed; otherwise PDF outcomes prefer `error`, `encrypted`, then `empty`. Derived-data fills written before `derived` existed read `ok` until repaired. Null before an attempt or derived-text fill.

Provenance of `text_content`. For `derived` rows, a JSON object `{comment_id, tool, available_tools, attachments:[{attachment, tool, key, size, etag, sha256}], only_in_other_tools}`: the primary tool (the first of `pypdf`, `pdfminer` with an object for the comment), every tool with an object for it, each attachment's tool, S3 key, listed size and ETag and the SHA-256 of the bytes read (null when the text was kept without re-reading them), and the attachment numbers taken from a tool other than the primary because the primary has no object for them (decision 41); those are in the text. A primary object that exists is kept even when blank. About 125 bytes plus 330 per attachment (31 KB at 92 attachments, the published maximum). Otherwise an ordered JSON array from the latest PDF attempt: `{url, source_sha256, status, page_count, error}` per distinct selected URL; SHA-256 identifies observed bytes, and no-bytes fetch failures have null digest/page count and a generic error. Null when neither is recorded.

The agency's own class for the submission (regulations.gov `subtype`), spelled as stated. It is agency-specific. EPA classifies the submitter: `Public Comment` (an individual), `Company/Organization Comment`, `Government Local`, `Government State`, `Government Federal`, `Government Tribal`, `Member of Congress`, `Mass Mail Campaign`, `Late Comment`. Most other agencies that state it put one generic label on every record (`Comment(s)`, `Public Comment`, FDA's `Electronic Regulation from Form`), and many state none. EPA's submitter classes also appear at other agencies in small numbers, and `Mass Mail Campaign` (and `Late Mass Mail Campaign`) at several, FWS among them; which agencies state which labels is a query (`SELECT agency_code, subtype, count(*) … GROUP BY ALL`), not a fixed list. Split organizations from individuals only within an agency that classifies, and not by `organization`: all 1,629 records of EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114 leave `organization`, `category` and `first_name` NULL, 219 of them `Company/Organization Comment`. NULL where the record states none or the row predates reading this field.

How many received submissions the agency says this posted record stands for (regulations.gov `duplicateComments`), as stated. Agencies that count (EPA and FWS among them) state 1 for a single comment and the campaign's size on a `Mass Mail Campaign` record (15,851 on EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114-1811, National Wildlife Federation Action Fund); agencies that do not count state 0 on every record. Rows are posted records. To estimate submissions, sum `GREATEST(duplicate_comments, 1)`, each posted record standing for at least itself, and first count the NULL rows: GREATEST reads NULL as 1. The sum counts the submissions the agency says its posted records stand for, each record at least itself: its posted accounting, not its official total. On the comments export of receipt sha256:77a08369… (2026-10-03), EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114's 1,629 records sum to 53,692, 52,086 of them on its 23 `Mass Mail Campaign` records, while EPA's response to comments reports about 122,200 received. The 2026-09-28 sample found it stated on every record: 0 on 5,281, 1 on 660, more than 1 on 4. NULL where the row predates reading this field; 0 is a stated zero.

`comment` read as plain text, derived from it each time the mirror is exported and never stored in the catalog. The publisher serves `comment` as an HTML fragment (`I'm`, `
`); this column decodes each character reference once, makes `
` and the end of a block element a newline and a no-break space a space, drops every other tag and trims the ends. Search and quote this column; `comment` keeps the publisher's bytes. The projection loses link targets, list bullets and table layout. One decode only: a body the publisher escaped twice keeps one level (`'` reads `'`), and markup a commenter typed as text (`<br>`) reads as that text. NULL exactly where `comment` is NULL.

agency_stats.coverage: Derived. Totals over `dockets`, `documents` and `comments`; it covers exactly what those cover.

columns.description: Agency short code. One row per agency.
Number of dockets posted by the agency.
Number of documents posted by the agency, less postings Regulations.gov removed (`documents.publisher_status`).

Posted comments on the agency's dockets, summed from `comments_index`, less those on a posting Regulations.gov removed. These are posted comment records, not comments received: an agency posts one record for a mass-mail campaign that can stand for thousands of submissions (EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114 has 1,629 posted records for about 122,200 comments EPA received). To estimate submissions received, sum `comments.duplicate_comments` as its description says; this table does not carry it.

fr_docket_links.label: Federal Register to docket links
fr_docket_links.summary: One Federal Register docket-reference occurrence, preserving printed docket labels and explicit Regulations.gov links separately. `link_source` names the source; repeated printed labels remain distinct. Printed agency labels are not automatically Regulations.gov identities. Qualified normalization candidates stay visible. Rulemaking grouping uses printed or both-source references only. Main Register number/date and docket values support exact navigation.
fr_docket_links.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: one link per docket a dated Federal Register record names, in its printed labels or in its regulations.gov link, over the `federal_register` table's own date range. A Register row not read since the regulations.gov link was first requested contributes its printed labels only.

columns.description: The docket as the statement gives it: a printed label verbatim from `docket_ids` (`Docket No. FAA-2007-29334`, an agency docket number, a `FRL-` number), or the Register's regulations.gov docket id.

Zero-based position of a printed label in the original docket array, before null/blank elements are filtered; NULL on a row the regulations.gov link alone carries. With document_number and publication_date it identifies a printed occurrence.
Literal Federal Register document number. Join to `federal_register` on both this value and `publication_date`; a number can name distinct dated records.
FR document title.
FR document abstract.
FR type: `Rule`, `Proposed Rule`, `Notice`, or `Presidential Document`.
FR subtype where the Federal Register supplies one, e.g. `Final Rule`, `Interim Final Rule`.
Date the document published in the Federal Register; required with `document_number` for the FR record join.
Date the rule takes effect, when the document carries one.
Comment period close date, when the document carries one.
Signing date, for presidential documents.
Federal Register agency slugs for the issuing agencies. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

The full original docket-ID array, retained so consumers can see the other IDs this FR document links to. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
RINs (Native list) claimed by the FR document — the RIN-side join key for a rulemaking. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
Executive order number, for presidential documents.

Which of the Register's statements carries the pair: `printed` (the document's printed docket labels), `regulations_dot_gov_info` (the Register's regulations.gov link, read from `regulations_dot_gov_docket_id` alone, never off a document id) or `both`, where a printed label is that docket id or SpicyDocs' normalizer reads it from the label. Every printed occurrence that carries the pair reads `both`, and the link then adds no row. The current builder writes one of these labels; retained historical rows without a label keep NULL.

fr_docket_links.subject: rulemaking
fr_docket_links.grain: One row per document–docket pair a dated Federal Register record states. Native receipt identity uses document_number, publication_date, literal docket_id and docket_source_ordinal: printed-array positions keep repeated labels distinct; the ordinal is NULL for a regulations.gov-only link, whose docket_id distinguishes the relationship. link_source is not part of the identity.

discovery_signals.label: Agency activity spikes
discovery_signals.summary: Per-agency document-output spike signal that powers the feed's discovery panel — agencies whose document count in the trailing 30 days is at least 2× their prior-year monthly mean, requiring ≥24 documents in the prior year to suppress tiny-denominator noise. Recomputed relative to the run date, so rows turn over on every rebuild; it is a current-state signal, not a time series. Built by `build_discovery_signals` from `documents`, less postings Regulations.gov removed (`documents.publisher_status`).
discovery_signals.coverage: Not a range. A dated snapshot recomputed from `documents` at each build. Its date is the calculation instant the file's metadata records (`spicy_regs.discovery_signals.as_of`, beside the date policy and the `documents` digest it read; `parquet_kv_metadata` on the generation's file returns them), not `measured_on`, which dates the audit of this note. Future dates are excluded from recent activity. This is not a historical series or a complete measure of agency activity. Receipt: fork-execution-2026-09-21/discovery-utc/MANUAL-AUDIT.md.
discovery_signals.data_quality: Activity windows use UTC instants and preserve explicit source offsets. Dates and timestamps without offsets use UTC; source values remain unchanged. Corpus backfills and source date anomalies can affect these document-count signals.

columns.description: Agency short code.
Documents the agency posted in the trailing 30 days.
Prior-year monthly mean document count (months 2–13 back).
`recent_30d` divided by `baseline` — the spike multiple.

cfr_sections.label: Code of Federal Regulations sections
cfr_sections.summary: One GovInfo annual CFR granule: a section, appendix or other structural unit. This is metadata, not regulatory body text. Enclosing parts come from annual volume PART headings, preserving compound and unusual numbering; printed section numbers alone do not identify a part. `cfr_ref` supplies the printed citation. Unchanged or unread volumes can retain earlier placement; the annual index package is excluded.
cfr_sections.coverage: Window. Annual-edition section metadata from the 2025 edition and, for some titles, the 2026 edition (`SELECT DISTINCT edition_year, title` lists which), not full publication history or body text. Each section's part comes from its volume's PART heading; on 2026-09-23 every compared Title 41, 43 and 14 section agreed with eCFR's 2025-01-01 structure. Receipts: fork-execution-2026-09-21/cfr-ancestry-fix-2026-09-23/ (candidate.json, validation.json).

columns.description: GovInfo granule identifier. Primary key / dedup key, including non-section structural units.

`'true'` on the granule that is a part itself (an id ending `-part200`, or `-part60-id334` in Title 41), `'false'` on every other row. A part's subparts, subject groups, appendices and table of contents share its `cfr_ref` and read `'false'`, so `part_granule = 'true'` picks the part out of them; a part citation's lookup does exactly that. Read from the granule id alone by SpicyDocs' grammar, never from the heading. A part held in two annual editions has one such row per edition, and a part printed across volumes one per volume (40 CFR part 60 spans volumes 7 to 9 of the 2025 edition).
GovInfo package identifier for the enclosing annual CFR title and volume.

Join key to Federal Register `cfr_references`. For a section, the title and its printed citation (e.g. `43-1601.0-1`, `41-50-201.1`); Title 43 keeps its subpart-numbered spelling while `part` names the enclosing part. The Federal Register side cuts every Title 41 compound part at the hyphen (`41 CFR 60-1.4` reads `41-60`), so a Title 41 reference there names a chapter, not a part, and matches no structural row here once the generation carries Title 41's compound parts (see the summary): match it at chapter level (`title = '41' AND part LIKE '60-%'`). NULL for ranges, publisher typos, unprefixed numbers (`Sec. 1-1`), parenthesized citations (`1.401(k)-1`), sections outside a numbered PART and section tokens the volume does not hold; 12 single sections printed with `§§` (`§§ 2.188`) are read as ranges until spicy-docs 0.31.0. For other granules, composed from the part and the identifier's tokens (e.g. `48-700`, `15-746.10-app1`); NULL without a part. A part-level reference (`40-60`) equals `cfr_ref` only on a part's structural rows, of which the part's own granule has `part_granule` `'true'`, and a part held only as sections has none (50 CFR 622 among 12 on 2026-10-03): match a part on `title` and `part`, which section rows carry.
CFR title number from the package or granule identifier (e.g. `40`).

For a section, the number in the enclosing PART heading of the package's annual volume XML (e.g. `1600`, `50-201`, `241`); NULL outside a numbered PART or when the volume does not hold the section. For a section's appendix or TOC (`sec746-10-app1`), its host section's part when the volume holds the host, else its token's leading number. For other granules, the identifier's part token including letter suffixes (e.g. `1203a`); in Title 41, whose identifiers cut a compound part at the hyphen, the compound part its part granule's heading states (`60-2`).

For a section, the printed number less its `{part}.` prefix (e.g. `1` for § 50-201.1, `19-8.1` in Part 241, `1601.0-1` in Part 1600, `401(k)-1`). For a section's appendix or TOC, the rest of its token after the leading number (`10-app1`); for a section token the volume does not hold, the whole token. NULL for other granules.
Granule heading / caption text from GovInfo's list-level `title` field.
GovInfo granule class / structural level (e.g. `CONTENT`, `NODE`, `TOC`, `APPENDIX`).
Annual edition year from the package or granule identifier, falling back to the year in `dateIssued`. This is not necessarily the printed body revision year or proof of a substantive edition.
Granule `lastModified` when supplied, otherwise the enclosing package's `lastModified`. GovInfo's granule listing supplies none, so in practice every row carries its package's stamp.

congress_bills.label: Congressional bills
congress_bills.summary: One bill or resolution. Full BILLSTATUS records, older API details and retained archive-list rows provide different amounts of detail. Pre-108th detail records do not include walked action, committee, text, subject or related-bill lists; their missing values stay NULL. `cosponsor_count` is retained when stated. Without actions, stage and signed-date rules remain unset. Main identifiers support navigation; source method and processing evidence are inspected separately.
congress_bills.coverage: True range on the archive index, mixed on enrichment. The index reaches the earliest Congresses, with latest actions from 1799-12-16. Scoped bill-family runs enrich the 108th Congress onward from GovInfo BILLSTATUS and the 82nd–107th from Congress.gov details. Older list-only rows can remain where enrichment has not run. Missing child records or CBO estimates do not prove source absence.
congress_bills.data_quality: **Historical cosponsor-count defect:** the 2026-09-21 native-XML audit found 13,154 wrong zero counts in the then-retained 118th Congress HR/S output using SpicyDocs 0.24.2. The current reader counts the publisher's separate cosponsors list, including withdrawn entries, as the column description states. Corrected code does not establish that every historical row has been re-read; consult the selected generation's audit before claiming population-wide repair. Historical receipt: `legislative-release-candidate-2026-09-21/`. `statutes_at_large_cite` is filled at this table's merge by joining the published `laws` table on `bill_id`, as its column sentence says: `bill-family` reads `laws` best-effort after its merge and takes the law's citation where one is published, keeping a citation already here where `laws` has none for the bill; with no `laws` table published the column stays as it was, NULL on a cold start. It is never guessed: `laws` publishes a citation only from a captured PLAW USLM file, and reads a NULL through its own `uslm_outcome`. `public_law_number` and `law_type` are not that case: they come from the bill's own publisher record — its `laws` entry, when the publisher states one — and are filled wherever the bill family has reached. `url_source` `congress_api_list` marks a row the retired list writer last wrote. Its run of 2026-09-23 replaced 3,044 BILLSTATUS `update_date` instants with the list route's same-day dates and 3,095 congress.gov page URLs with API resource URLs (receipt `drift-audit-2026-09-23/`). The bill family re-reads every such bill in its scope instead of skipping it as unchanged, so the current Congress's rows heal on its next run; the 47 rows it relabelled in the 114th–118th (five of the replaced URLs among them) are re-read only by a run scoped to their Congress. `update_date` merges by the larger value, so a re-read never moves it backwards; the 46 rows of the 119th (and 42 older) whose list date is later than BILLSTATUS's therefore keep that date-only value after the re-read, and until BILLSTATUS catches up they read `url_source` `billstatus` beside an `update_date` no BILLSTATUS document stated. Each run reads stage and signing date again from the stored actions, so a rule change needs no re-read. The 26 BILLSTATUS bills of the 108th-111th and 117th that stayed in doubt after every read on 2026-09-29 list a printing twice or without a type, so their `version_count` exceeds their `bill_versions` rows.

columns.description: Natural key: congress, bill type and number joined with hyphens (119-hr-6028).
The numbered Congress this measure belongs to.
Lowercase publisher bill or resolution type (hr, s, hjres, sres...).
The measure's number within its Congress and type.
The measure's official title as BILLSTATUS states it.
The chamber the measure originated in, as the publisher states it.
Date of the publisher's own latestAction entry.
Text of the publisher's own latestAction entry.
The publisher's updateDate for this record; the merge prefers the larger value.
The publisher's updateDateIncludingText, which moves when a text version posts.
The date the measure was introduced, as the publisher states it.
The publisher's single policy-area term for this measure.
Every legislative subject term the publisher lists, as a Native list in publisher order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
How many legislative subject terms the publisher listed.
Bioguide id of the first sponsor the publisher lists.
Full name string of the first sponsor, exactly as the publisher spells it.
Number of items in the publisher's separate cosponsors list, including withdrawn entries; NULL when that list was not examined.
Action code of the actions[] entry the publisher's latestAction names; latestAction itself states no code, so the two are linked on date and text.
The publisher's actionTime on the latestAction entry.
How many action entries this document carries; the bill_actions row count for this bill.

How many committees and subcommittees this document names, at any nesting depth.  This is the bill_committees row count except where the publisher states a committee with no systemCode, which cannot be keyed and is refused.
How many text versions this BILLSTATUS document offers.  Not the bill_versions row count: a PDF twin and an upload are rows the publisher's own list does not name.
Public law number from the publisher's laws entry, when the measure became a public law; NULL on a private law (law_type says which; its number is laws.law_number).
The publisher's law type for the first laws entry (Public Law or Private Law).

NULL here on purpose: the citation is published on laws.statutes_at_large_cite, read from the PLAW USLM meta, and the host fills this column by joining laws on bill_id at merge time. The family build sees one BILLSTATUS document and its printings; the PLAW is a different package the laws rollup acquires once per law, so filling it here would fetch every PLAW twice or read another table's output, which the one-pass rule forbids.

The whole bill's interpreted legislative stage: the latest step its actions show under the current rule, not a final outcome. On the ladder: `introduced`, `committee`, `calendared`, `passed_chamber`, `other_chamber`, `passed_both`, `conference`, `cleared`, `presented` or `law` (the terminal rung; the literal is `law`, never `enacted`); or an outcome with no rung, `failed` or `vetoed`. `introduced` is also the default when no rule fires (see stage_rule); NULL where the bill's actions were not examined, which is not a statement about enactment. A number the House reserves for its leadership (title "Reserved for the Speaker.") has no actions: it reads `introduced` with stage_rule NULL, or NULL where GovInfo holds no document. A mention is not an event: taking over the sponsorship of a bill "originally introduced by" another, a floor action citing the text "as introduced" or "as reported", a special rule's report or description, and a star print classify nothing, and where the publisher's action code names a step, the code is read before the text. `calendared` is a placement on the Union, House or Senate Legislative Calendar in the bill's own chamber (a reported bill awaiting the floor, or one placed there unreported under Senate Rule XIV or a discharge); a later report, order to report, subcommittee referral or floor step leaves it `calendared`, and only a referral of the bill to a committee lowers it. `passed_chamber` and `other_chamber` both mean the bill's own chamber has passed it; `other_chamber` adds that the other chamber has received it or taken a calendar, desk or floor step on it. A calendar placement, the desk, a motion to proceed or cloture reads `other_chamber` only where the chamber that took it (as the text names it, else the system that entered it) is not the one the bill's type originates in; in its own chamber the desk, a motion to proceed or cloture moves nothing. `passed_both` means both chambers have passed it (the Library of Congress's 8000 and 17000 where the actions carry codes, else the text) but not, as far as the wording shows, in one text: the second passage carried an amendment the other chamber has not agreed to, or names none either way (the House's "On passage Passed"), and the publisher lists no enrolled text. It is read from the passage that completed it. `conference` is a conference requested, held or reported; the Library of Congress's "Resolving differences" exchange of amendments is not one. `cleared` means both chambers have agreed to one text: the second chamber passed it as it arrived (the Senate "without amendment", or the House on a motion to suspend the rules that names no amendment), a chamber agreed to the other's amendment with no amendment of its own, or both agreed to a conference report; the Library of Congress's "Cleared for White House." (109th-111th Congresses) reads it too. So does a measure both chambers passed in wording that states no agreement (the House's "On agreeing to the resolution Agreed to" on a Senate concurrent resolution) where its BILLSTATUS document lists an enrolled text, GPO's final copy of a measure both chambers passed in identical form. A bill or joint resolution is then ready for the President; a concurrent resolution is complete. `failed` is the latest vote on passage failing in either chamber, a failed two-thirds vote to suspend the rules included: the measure can still pass, and it reads over an earlier passage by the other chamber until a later step. `vetoed` stands until a recorded enactment; a failed override keeps it. The stage never moves back once a chamber has passed the bill: the other chamber's referral or report, a star print or an introduction phrase does not lower it, and only a passage the Senate states it vitiated is undone; where the actions carry publisher codes, the Library of Congress's passage code (8000 House, 17000 Senate) is what holds it. Once `cleared`, no lower rung moves it back. A motion's or a point of order's result ("motion to proceed ... agreed to in Senate") is not the measure's passage, and "disagreed to in Senate" reads `failed`.

Which rule fired: a stage's own name where that rule read the action's text (`introduced`, `committee`, `calendared`, `passed_chamber`, `other_chamber`, `conference`, `cleared`, `presented`, `law`), `cleared` also for both chambers' agreement to a conference report, read from the second; `vetoed` for the President's veto; `failed_passage` for a failed vote on passage, a failed veto override included (which leaves the stage `vetoed`); `action_code` where the Library of Congress's passage or presentation code decided it; `became_law_code` for the publisher's became-law code; `passed_both` for the passage that left both chambers' passages standing; `enrolled_text_listed` for `cleared` read from the enrolled text the BILLSTATUS document lists, not from an action. NULL when no rule fired and the default stood.
The full action text the stage rule matched against, never shortened; for enrolled_text_listed, the listed text version's type as the publisher states it ("Enrolled Bill").
The date of the publisher's coded became-law action (36000, E40000 or the BecameLaw type) for a public or a private law; NULL where the bill states no law, or states one with no coded action.

Which signed-date rule produced that answer: `public_law_and_became_law_action`, `private_law_and_became_law_action`, `public_law_without_became_law_action` (a public law with no coded action, so no date) or `no_public_law` (no law entry, or a private law with no coded action).

Interpreted money-bill kind, or NULL when no rule claimed the measure. A title heuristic with unmeasured recall: an appropriations act whose title lacks the pattern, or an appropriations division inside another bill, is NULL (money_bill_rule names the rule that fired). A simple or concurrent resolution (H. Res., S. Res., H. Con. Res., S. Con. Res.) is never a money bill, though a House special rule names the one it brings up, and `omnibus` is an appropriations omnibus only, not a statute named "Omnibus" (the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act).

Fiscal year the display title states, spelled FY plus the year: `fiscal year 2027`, the long title's `for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027`, or an appropriations act's closing year (`... Appropriations Act, 2027`, `Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027`). Never read from short_title, which a reused vehicle takes from the act it replaced. NULL where the title states none.

Which of the twelve appropriations subcommittees the title names, under the statutory names: the House's National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs reads `State, Foreign Operations`. Read only where the regular-appropriations rule (or a manual override) classified the bill.

The publisher's short title for the whole measure: the first titles[] entry whose titleType names a short title, which is the newest stage's because the publisher lists titles newest stage first, skipping the types that name only portions of the bill (an omnibus's divisions); NULL where the measure states no short title for the whole of it, which is ordinary.

columns.column_type: STRUCT(bill_type VARCHAR, congress VARCHAR, latest_action_date VARCHAR, latest_action_text VARCHAR, number VARCHAR, relationship_details STRUCT(identifiedBy VARCHAR, "type" VARCHAR)[], title VARCHAR)[]
columns.description: Every relatedBills entry the publisher states, as a Native list, with each one's relationship details nested; this replaces BillTrax's hand-set related_bill_id with the publisher's own fact. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
How many related bills the publisher states.

congress_bills.subject: congress
congress_bills.grain: One row per bill or resolution, as one BILLSTATUS document states it.

bill_subjects.label: Bill policy areas and legislative subjects
bill_subjects.summary: One policy-area and subject-list assignment per bill, from Congress.gov or GovInfo BILLSTATUS. Join on `bill_id`. Subject names are filter values, not separate bill records. Native rows use `subjects`; legacy rows use `subjects_json`. Acquisition method and time belong to receipts for native rows; legacy rows retain `carrier` and `enriched_at`.
bill_subjects.coverage: Sampled. Subject assignments for bills from the 93rd Congress onward. From the 108th, assignments come from held BILLSTATUS rows or bulk archives; earlier bills and refused bulk records use the keyed Congress.gov API, up to 2,000 a run. Bulk reads cover 32 folders per run, newest first; no new request starts after 20 minutes. Missing bills may be pending, refused or outside the run's scope.
bill_subjects.data_quality: A missing row can mean pending, failed or outside the configured scope. An empty assignment can mean no assignments or that the source did not hold the requested bill; those outcomes are not separately represented in this table. Rows copied from the bill family are rewritten when the family's BILLSTATUS read changes; other answers are not asked again. The table does not retain the original response or its digest.

columns.description: Stable bill key shared with congress_bills.bill_id, such as 119-hr-1. Primary/dedup key; join by this identifier rather than title.
Publisher policy-area name after trimming, or NULL when the returned answer has no policy area.

Native list of trimmed, deduplicated legislative subject names. An empty array alone does not distinguish unassigned from not held. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
Length of subjects, stored as a decimal string; not a count of bills or independent source responses.

bill_subjects.subject: congress
bill_subjects.grain: One observed subject assignment per bill_id, with the latest retained answer replacing its predecessor.

unified_agenda.label: Planned agency actions
unified_agenda.summary: One row per Regulation Identifier Number (RIN) per agenda edition, ingested from the OIRA/OMB Unified Agenda published at reginfo.gov by `build_unified_agenda`. A Tier-1 rulemaking-lifecycle source: the upstream, forward-looking catalog of rulemakings agencies *plan* to pursue, keyed by the same `rin` that appears in `federal_register` (`regulation_id_numbers`). Primary / dedup key is (`rin`, `agenda_edition`).
unified_agenda.coverage: True range: the retained published baseline starts at 199510 and excludes the 2004 editions and spring 2012; agenda_edition names each included edition. A local source-only replay now recovers the two 2004 editions through narrowly qualified repairs; that candidate has not been published. See docs/unified-agenda-retained-rebuild.md for the qualification boundary. A rule has one row per edition that lists it, so count distinct rin, not rows, for a number of rules.

columns.description: Regulation Identifier Number (e.g. `2060-AV12`). The RIN join key to `federal_register`. Half of the primary/dedup key.
Short code of the agency that owns the RIN.
Full name of the agency that owns the RIN.
Title of the planned rulemaking.
Agency-written abstract describing the planned action. Often null.
Status of the RIN in this edition (e.g. `Active`, `Completed`, `Long-Term`).
Stage of the rulemaking in this edition (e.g. `Prerule`, `Proposed Rule`, `Final Rule`).
OIRA priority classification (e.g. `Economically Significant`, `Other Significant`, `Substantive, Nonsignificant`).

Semiannual agenda edition the row was published in, as reginfo.gov's `pubId` `YYYYMM`: MM 04 and 10 are its spring and fall editions, except that reginfo.gov titles 202510 the "2026" agenda (202504 is Spring 2025). The month is not a release date: an edition appears months later (USDA printed 202510 in the Register on 2026-08-14), and no release date is held. Half of the primary/dedup key. Every readable edition since 199510 is held, so filter to one edition, or count distinct `rin`, before counting rules.
Whether the action is a major rule, as reported by the agenda (e.g. `Yes`/`No`). Often null.
reginfo.gov publication identifier for this agenda entry, when present.

columns.column_type: STRUCT("action" VARCHAR, date VARCHAR, fr_citation VARCHAR)[]
columns.description: Native list of planned and actual milestone actions with literal source dates and Federal Register citations. A date with day 00 has month precision; labels such as To Be Determined remain unchanged. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
Native list of CFR citations affected by the rulemaking. The join key to the CFR. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

Earliest distinct calendar date derived from the timetable, or NULL when none is derivable. Source month-only dates (MM/00/YYYY) use day 01 here; timetable retains their original precision.

comment_periods.label: Derived submission-date windows
comment_periods.summary: One rule-derived group of source-reported comment windows. Extension/reopening language links windows only when an explicit page citation or qualified RIN uniquely identifies an overlapping or adjoining earlier notice. Conflicts do not link; a gap starts another period. These are candidate groupings, not verified legal extensions. Docket/proceeding anchors never merge groups, and synthetic Federal Register feed dockets anchor none. Ordered source references support navigation.
comment_periods.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: every `federal_register` record with a `comments_close_on`, every `documents` row with a comment end date, and every Register record such a document copies lands in exactly one period, anchored or not. Left out are windows that close before they open, placeholder closes (see data quality), and legacy Regulations.gov documents that state a comment end but neither a comment start nor a posting date (all closing by 2011); the builder logs each count. Live row counts come from `describe_table`.
comment_periods.data_quality: For date-range discovery, test all three date columns (`close_date`, `register_close_date` and `regulations_gov_close_date`). They can concern different purposes, including comments, replies, objections, hearings or petitions; the builder does not classify legal submission purpose. `close_date` is the maximum normalized close among grouped records, not the legally controlling/current deadline. The source-specific columns retain each source's maximum; a difference is not resolved by choosing the later value. Base Federal Register dates remain historical statements of each dated publication, not current status, and Regulations.gov records can update independently. Inspect source filing instructions and later notices; neither title matching nor a shared docket/RIN proves legal effect. Extension/correction documents with NULL dates can exist outside these windows, and NULL does not establish no deadline. A close on or after 2050-01-01 is a placeholder and states nothing: the inputs hold no close from 2033 to 2049, and every later one is a stand-in (Regulations.gov's 2099 and 2100 dates, FDA's 2050-02-21 open dockets, Register year typos such as 3008 for 2008). A record whose only close is a placeholder, or whose window closes before it opens, adds no dates; it is listed only as its notice's Register record when a copy states a window. The formal rulespec export is the anchored rows (`anchor_kind <> 'none'`), since rulespec's CommentPeriod needs a proceeding or docket anchor; no export exists yet. A Regulations.gov document is a notice's copy only when its `fr_doc_num` says so, so a copy that omits it stands as its own notice: on the 2026-09-28 inputs about 2,950 such documents share a docket, close day and opening (within three days) with a Register notice. An extension stays its own period when it names its notice by neither page nor RIN, when its title says "extension of time for comments" (the title matcher misses that phrasing), or when its page or RINs name more than one open notice: one extension of two proposals (2022-13209 extends 2022-08993 and 2022-08994 under RINs 0910-AI28 and 0910-AI60) links to neither. A legacy Regulations.gov document whose posting date is decades early (see `documents`) opens its period that early.

rulemaking_lifecycles.label: Rulemaking lifecycles
rulemaking_lifecycles.summary: One docketed proceeding's proposal-to-final history and survival outcome. The earliest Register-dated proposal takes precedence over an upload-dated proposal; the final must follow it strictly. Other events determine the outcome or censor date. Docket-less Register records cannot pair and are excluded. Unified Agenda status and routine strata remain separate context. These are docketed proceedings, not a count of distinct RINs or regulations.
rulemaking_lifecycles.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: every docketed proceeding, paired from its cleaned `lifecycle_events` and censored at the day its inputs end.
rulemaking_lifecycles.data_quality:
A Regulations.gov document that states no Register number in `fr_doc_num`, or whose stated number resolves to no Register row, is dated by its upload, which for a legacy document can be years after the rule: on snapshot_9b2c770e's inputs 262 lifecycles anchor on such a document, 74 of them upload pairs outside survival (docs/ontology.md). A proposal typed only by Regulations.gov (`lifecycle_events.source = 'regulations_gov'`, an unnumbered upload) can be a petition for rulemaking, a state program submission or an information-collection notice the Register files under another type: on snapshot_62318069's inputs 515 survival lifecycles since 2015 anchor on one (352 open); a Register number its title names is not read as its identity. Where the proceeding also holds the Register's proposal, the Register's anchors (54d); an upload keeps its anchor when a final falls between the two or the Register's is a comment-period extension or correction, so an earlier proposal whose Register copy is missing may still anchor on its later re-proposal (FDA's 1978 OTC-monograph dockets re-proposed in the 1990s). A final that finalizes another docket's proposal is paired in its own proceeding only and the proposal stays `open`: a RIN never groups dockets (56a), and the Register's docket labels are often an agency's own (2026-15833 names 'CMS-1849-F and CMS-0062-F' and no RIN). A Register proposal naming several dockets anchors one lifecycle per docket (502 proposals behind 2,358 of 35,327 survival rows on snapshot_62318069's inputs; EPA 20%). A posting Regulations.gov flags withdrawn (`documents.withdrawn`) anchors nothing: it was misfiled, duplicated, moved or replaced, and the Register publishes an agency's withdrawal of a rule as a document of its own.
For `routine_family` `pesticide_tolerance` the proposal is usually EPA's notice that it received a pesticide petition (FFDCA 408(d)(3)), typed Proposed Rule, not a proposal of rule text: 443 of the 459 EPA tolerance lifecycles proposed since 2020 on snapshot_448e6d9a's inputs. Time to final then runs from the receipt notice, and `proposal_form` does not tell the two apart.
FDA's notices that it filed a food or color additive petition ("Filing of Food Additive Petition", "… Color Additive Petition") are the same case with no stratum: the Register types them Proposed Rule (its `action`, "Notification of petition.", is not carried by `federal_register`), `routine_family` is NULL, and on snapshot_55d396ee's inputs 64 of the 199 FDA lifecycles proposed since 2018, and 130 of the 831 in the published FDA cell, anchor on one. Match the proposal's Register title (`filing of … petition`) to set them apart. A count of lifecycles counts docketed proceedings, not rulemakings: FNA's three open lifecycles on that snapshot are one RIN, 0584-AF22, in dockets FNA-2026-0034, -0166 and -0201; count distinct `proceedings.rin` for rulemakings.

Day of the withdrawal that makes it `withdrawn`; NULL otherwise.
The withdrawal: a dated Register record id, or the agenda item id (`urn:rkaf:us:rin:<rin>`) of an Agenda withdrawal.
Its survival outcome: `final`, `withdrawn` (a competing outcome) or `censored`; NULL for a kind outside survival.

sam_entities.label: Federal entity registry
sam_entities.summary: One row per active SAM.gov registration, ingested from the Entity Management API v4 bulk extract (`/entities?format=json`) by `build_sam_entities`. The authoritative federal entity registry, the directory of organizations registered to do business with or receive assistance from the U.S. government. Its UEI is the identity `usaspending_recipients.uei` joins on. Comments carry no UEI, so a commenting organization reaches this table only by a name match on `legal_business_name` or `dba_name`, which is not an identity. Filtered to public active registrations (`registrationStatus=A`); list-level fields only.
sam_entities.coverage: Window, complete for the years read. Every public active registration SAM.gov dated 1996 through 2026 and the two older ones (1949, 1968), one bulk extract per registrationDate year; each year matched its active count when read, less its credited renewals (see data_quality), and the output ledger records the counts. Scheduled runs re-read the current year every other day and cycle through the older years between, and each year read replaces that year's rows.
sam_entities.data_quality: A row is a registration, keyed by `uei` and `entity_eft_indicator`: one entity registers once per EFT indicator (187 of the 147,038 UEIs in the 2026 extract carry more than one), so `uei` alone is not unique. SAM keeps a renewed registration's prior record Active until its expiry is processed, and counts both; the table keeps the newer, and the reader credits the other toward the file's declared count (one each in 2007, 2008, 2011, 2013, 2019 and 2020 and two in 2026, each journaled). A file with fewer registrations than it declares, less those credits, is refused. A year read retires the registrations it no longer holds (80 expired from 2002 and 2003 and 11 from 2026 on 2026-09-26), journaled as `rows-retired` so qualification reconciles every removal. A stalled extract is abandoned and triggered afresh, each abandonment journaled.

lobbying_filings.label: Lobbying disclosure filings
lobbying_filings.summary: One row per federal lobbying-disclosure filing, ingested from the U.S. Senate Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA) REST API (`lda.gov`, formerly `lda.senate.gov`) by `build_lobbying_filings`. Registrants file quarterly reports naming the clients they lobby for, the money involved, the issues raised, and the government entities (agencies/chambers) lobbied — so this table links the comment campaigns in `comments`/`dockets` to the same organizations' *direct* agency lobbying. Primary / dedup key is `filing_uuid`.
lobbying_filings.coverage: Sampled from retained Senate Lobbying Disclosure Act API captures. The snapshot has known gaps in filing years 1999–2006. Later filings may be absent. Some posting dates supplied by the publisher are anomalous.
lobbying_filings.data_quality: Filing years 1999-2006 are short of the LDA's declared totals: offset paging over tied posting times skipped 12,853 filings in the one walk held (measured 2026-10-30, filings missing of declared): 1999 2,099 of 31,498; 2000 584 of 31,555; 2001 676 of 35,897; 2002 1,429 of 38,352; 2003 2,669 of 43,292; 2004 1,969 of 44,704; 2005 2,180 of 49,353; 2006 1,247 of 49,068. Filing years 2007 to 2025 matched their declared totals.

columns.description: LDA filing UUID (e.g. `7866327b-c892-4430-b9f0-1f0f679c58c6`). Primary key / dedup key.

The LDA filing-type code as the API states it: `RR` registration; `Q1`–`Q4` quarterly reports and `MM` the pre-2008 mid-year report; `1A`–`4A` and `MA` amendments; `1T`–`4T` and `MT` terminations; `1@`–`4@` and `M@` termination amendments; a trailing `Y` marks a no-activity report (`Q1Y`, `1@Y`). The LDA constants endpoint (`/api/v1/constants/filing/filingtypes/`) is the authority. An amendment is a separate filing that restates its quarter's report. To total amounts, drop registrations (`RR`, `RA`), which carry a `filing_period` too, then keep the latest filing per registrant, `client_id` and period: with registrations kept, a later one displaced a quarterly report in 103 groups of 2025 (measured 2026-10-03). For issues or activities, choose filing types first: a termination chain (`1T`, then a no-activity `1@Y`) shares the period, and the latest filing can be the no-activity one.
Calendar year the filing reports on.
Reporting period within the year (e.g. `first_quarter`, `year_end`).
Timestamp the filing was posted to the LDA system (ISO 8601 string with timezone). Sort key.
Name of the registrant (the lobbying firm or self-filing organization).
LDA registrant id. Stable join key across a registrant's filings.

The client's name as the registrant filed it; a name, not an identity. A self-filing organization is both registrant and client, often under a spelling other registrants do not use for it (McKesson files as `MCKESSON CORPORATION & AFFILIATES …`). `registrant_id` keys the registrant across its filings and `client_id` keys a client only within one registrant (see `client_id`); a match to `comments.organization` or `sam_entities.legal_business_name` is a name match.

LDA's `client.id`: one registrant's record of one client, stable across that registrant's filings, not an organization identity. No id is shared between registrants (129,434 ids for 129,434 registrant-client pairs, measured 2026-10-03), so an organization hired by several firms has one id per firm (AT&T Services, Inc.: 21 ids under 21 registrants in 2025).

Lobbying income reported by a lobbying firm for the period, in USD. Null for self-filers (who report `expenses`). An amended report (`filing_type` `1A`–`4A`) restates its quarter's amount, often unchanged, so summing over every filing counts that quarter twice; drop registrations (`RR`, `RA`) and keep the latest filing per registrant, `client_id` and quarter (see `filing_type`).

Lobbying expenses reported by a self-filing organization for the period, in USD. Null for firms (who report `income`). An amended report (`filing_type` `1A`–`4A`) restates its quarter's amount, often unchanged, so summing over every filing counts that quarter twice; drop registrations (`RR`, `RA`) and keep the latest filing per registrant, `client_id` and quarter (see `filing_type`). A self-filing organization's expenses already include what it pays outside lobbying firms, whose `income` for that client is reported separately; do not add the two.

columns.column_type: STRUCT(general_issue_code VARCHAR, general_issue_code_display VARCHAR, description VARCHAR)[]
columns.description: Native list of lobbying activities, each `{general_issue_code, general_issue_code_display, description}` — the issue areas lobbied and their free-text descriptions. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

Government entities named on the filing, in order of first appearance. A rebuilt filing lists each source ID once and uses the source name when the ID is absent. The activity rows retain every occurrence. Earlier native generations may repeat entities at filing level. A missing activity list yields null and an empty activity list yields an empty result.
The publisher's label for `filing_type`, as served (e.g. `1st Quarter - Report`, `Registration`).
The publisher's label for `filing_period`, as served (e.g. `1st Quarter (Jan 1 - Mar 31)`).
Media type of the filing document at `url`, as LDA states it (e.g. `text/html`, `application/pdf`); null on the few filings that state none.

The self-filer's expense accounting method code as filed (`expenses_method`). Two spellings occur, both kept as filed: lower case `a`, `b`, `c`, whose `expenses_method_display` is the long label, and upper case `A`, `B`, `C`, whose display is the bare letter; both occur in current years (a 400-page retained sample, 2026-10-30, held 751 lower-case and 286 upper-case codes). `a`/`A` is Method A (LDA definitions), `b`/`B` Method B (IRC 6033(b)(8)), `c`/`C` Method C (IRC 162(e)). Null when the filing states no method, as on most firm reports, which carry `income` instead.

The publisher's label for `expenses_method`, as filed: `Method A - Reporting amounts using LDA definitions only`, `Method B - Reporting amounts under section 6033(b)(8) of the Internal Revenue Code`, `Method C - Reporting amounts under section 162(e) of the Internal Revenue Code`, or the bare letter when the code is upper case.
Date the registrant ended its representation of the client, on a termination report (`filing_type` `1T`–`4T`, `MT` and their no-activity forms). Null on other filings.
Name of the person who signed and posted the filing, as entered (often with a title, e.g. `Frank J. Donatelli, Senior Advisor`).
First line of the registrant's address as filed on this filing. The address can differ between a registrant's filings; it is the filing's own, not a current registrant profile.
Second line of the registrant's address as filed on this filing; null when none was filed.
City of the registrant's address as filed on this filing.
State code of the registrant's address as filed on this filing (e.g. `DC`); null for an address outside the United States.
ZIP or postal code of the registrant's address as filed on this filing.
Country of the registrant's address as filed on this filing, as the publisher displays it (e.g. `United States of America`), not a country code.
Country of the registrant's principal place of business as filed, when the filing states one (display name); null otherwise.
The filing's flag for whether the registrant's principal place of business differs from the address filed: true, false, or null when the filing does not carry it (registrations among others).

fec_committees.label: Political committees
fec_committees.summary: One row per observed Federal Election Commission committee. The current reader acquires from the unfiltered OpenFEC `/v1/committees/` endpoint through SpicyDocs; the delivered seed's selected scope is stated above. SpicyRegs preserves the registry's fields, merges complete fresh traversals with prior observations by committee_id, and lets a fresh whole row replace its prior row. Raw page captures and acquisition manifests remain in FEC_CAPTURE_DIR. This identity/reference table can join other records carrying an FEC committee identifier. The company, union or association behind a PAC (FEC's connected organization) is not a column here: join `fec_committee_history` on committee_id and read `connected_organization_name`, one value per two-year cycle as that cycle's committee master states it (take the latest cycle for the current sponsor). first_file_date and last_file_date are dates, cycles and candidate_ids are native lists, and the other columns are text.

The OpenFEC committee registry: the whole registry is walked every Sunday (decision 53) and committees that filed in the last week are read daily; rows only an earlier walk saw are kept. first_file_date and last_file_date describe filing activity, not acquisition.

fec_source_records.label: Original FEC source records
fec_source_records.summary: Joinable metadata and retained source evidence across FEC families. collection_id joins fec_collections; source_family joins fec_source_catalog. Rows from different files and election cycles share this table, which has no cycle column: join collection_id to the fec_collection_cycles view for the cycle (2026 means 2025-2026) before comparing with a cycle's totals. A transaction's type, direction, other party, amount and memo flag are fields inside metadata_json (TRANSACTION_TP, OTHER_ID, CAND_ID, TRANSACTION_AMT, MEMO_CD). Native identifiers are lifted only when the provider reports them, and committee_id can join fec_committees. metadata_json and source_record_json preserve the complete provider record. PostgreSQL metadata additionally exposes named_fields from its verified schema; raw COPY fields, decoded NULLs and array text remain separate. Missing IDs remain missing.
fec_source_records.coverage: Sampled. The records of the selected collections in fec_collections, not complete FEC history. Inspect each collection's retained selection and source coordinates before combining observations. An archive's main file, date partitions and correction files can overlap; physical source rows are not a deduplicated transaction population.
fec_source_records.data_quality: Memo, subtotal and attribution fields retain their source meaning. Their eligibility depends on the source family, retained definitions and analytic purpose; no blanket memo exclusion applies to every query. Joint fundraising transfer and attribution observations can overlap without carrying an exact source link between them. Monetary values, amendment chains and record inclusion rules differ by family; generic record ingestion does not select a latest amendment or establish a safe sum. Unknown fields stay in native JSON. Original pinned bytes preserve numeric spelling where the provider exposes exact decimal values as strings.

columns.description: Zero-based source occurrence position within this generation. Repeated source records retain distinct positions; the ordinal is not a stable identity across generations.

Selected collection label: the file or query the record came from. Together with source_record_id identifies this record; joins fec_collections.collection_id and, for the election cycle, fec_collection_cycles.collection_id.
Caller-selected official FEC source-family identifier, checked against the inventory. Joins fec_source_catalog.source_family; this classification is not independently inferred from source content.
Provider reader profile used to interpret the verified input.

Committee ID as the source reports it (bulk CMTE_ID or the API's committee_id). In transaction files this is the committee that filed the report, not necessarily the one that received the money: a PAC's contribution to a candidate is filed under the PAC's ID, with the recipient in metadata_json OTHER_ID and CAND_ID, and TRANSACTION_TP says which way the money moved. To find money a committee received from other committees, also search OTHER_ID: in the 2025-2026 file a candidate committee's own filings list no direct PAC contributions, so they appear only under each PAC's committee_id, with the candidate in OTHER_ID and CAND_ID (TRANSACTION_TP 24K). May join fec_committees.committee_id. Blanks remain blank; no identifier is inferred from a name or another entity's ID.

Literal candidate identifier reported by API metadata or a verified named bulk field such as CAND_ID. Blanks and aggregate codes remain literal; an ID-shaped aggregate value does not establish a person. Names are not converted to identifiers.

JSON source coordinates identifying the original response field, record, file or ZIP member and byte span when supplied. Optional field_mapping pins the selected source header or HTML field dictionary; complete dictionary cells appear in the parent collection's tableFieldDefinitions.

fec_account_transfers.label: Reported transfers between accounts
fec_account_transfers.summary: One source-reported account-transfer or allocated-activity record version. Keeps transferred amounts, activity amounts and totals separate. An account transfer is not automatically a receipt to the reporting committee or a payment to a third party. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row comes from `fec-electronic-filing-schedule`.
fec_account_transfers.coverage: Sampled. Supported observations from retained Schedule H3/H5 account-transfer and activity layouts. The retained selection is explicit in fec_collections and its source-generation evidence; this declaration does not establish complete FEC history or current publication.
fec_account_transfers.data_quality: Exact decimals preserve signs. Memo, subtotal and attribution flags require source-specific interpretation; successful mapping does not qualify current, gross or net totals. Keep reported balances, allocation totals/components, overlapping summaries and two-sided transfers at their declared grains. Quality notices do not automatically exclude records.

fec_allocation_bases.label: Reported allocation basis observations
fec_allocation_bases.summary: One source-reported allocation method, ratio or supporting-basis record version. Makes source ratios, percentage text, ballot points and supporting amounts inspectable. These are allocation bases and do not create additional payment events. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row comes from `fec-electronic-filing-schedule`.
fec_allocation_bases.coverage: Sampled. Supported observations from retained Schedule H1/H2 allocation layouts. The retained selection is explicit in fec_collections and its source-generation evidence; this declaration does not establish complete FEC history or current publication.
fec_allocation_bases.data_quality: Exact decimals preserve signs. Memo, subtotal and attribution flags require source-specific interpretation; successful mapping does not qualify current, gross or net totals. Keep reported balances, allocation totals/components, overlapping summaries and two-sided transfers at their declared grains. Quality notices do not automatically exclude records.

Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence.

fec_debts.data_quality: Exact decimals preserve signs. Memo, subtotal and attribution flags require source-specific interpretation; successful mapping does not qualify current, gross or net totals. Keep reported balances, allocation totals/components, overlapping summaries and two-sided transfers at their declared grains. Quality notices do not automatically exclude records.

legacy_column_descriptions.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the original source witness bytes; distinct from the typed table's publication digest.

legacy_column_descriptions.filing_key: Nullable authority- and namespace-qualified filing-version key. Several retained observations can share it; group proven filing identity before joining. fec_disbursements.label: Reported disbursement observations
fec_disbursements.summary: One source-reported payment or disbursement record version. Retains payment amount, payee, purpose, codes and memo fields. Refunds, transfers and other source types keep their own meanings; mapping does not select current amendments or a net spending total. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row has the amount status `exact`.
fec_disbursements.coverage: Sampled. Supported observations from retained bulk operating-expense files, supported Schedule B layouts and payment APIs. The retained selection is explicit in fec_collections and its source-generation evidence; this declaration does not establish complete FEC history or current publication.
fec_disbursements.data_quality: Exact decimals preserve signs. Memo, subtotal and attribution flags require source-specific interpretation; successful mapping does not qualify current, gross or net totals. Keep reported balances, allocation totals/components, overlapping summaries and two-sided transfers at their declared grains. Quality notices do not automatically exclude records.

fec_electioneering_communications.summary: One source candidate-associated disbursement observation. Keeps each candidate association, the full disbursement amount and the publisher-calculated candidate share. Similar dates/payees/images do not prove a shared event key; unresolved event equivalence prevents summing full amounts once per candidate. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. fec_electioneering_communications.data_quality: Exact decimals preserve signs. Memo, subtotal and attribution flags require source-specific interpretation; successful mapping does not qualify current, gross or net totals. Keep reported balances, allocation totals/components, overlapping summaries and two-sided transfers at their declared grains. Quality notices do not automatically exclude records.

fec_filing_links.label: Source-reported filing-version references
fec_filing_links.summary: One directed native filing reference from a retained filing observation. Follow explicit source references without selecting a latest report.
