fec_independent_expenditures.label: Reported independent-expenditure observations
fec_independent_expenditures.summary: One source-reported independent-expenditure record version. Separates spender, payee, candidate target, expenditure date, dissemination date and report metadata. Generic spender_name, payee_name, candidate_name and expenditure_date apply only to layouts that supply those fields. Original-filing Schedule E rows instead retain payee organization/person-name fields, candidate name components, and separate dissemination_date, disbursement_date and signed_date. For an original-filing row, the filing's cover is the fec_filing_report_observations row with the same collection_id and `report_record_role` `reported-form`; its form_type ends N for a new filing and A for an amendment (`F24N`, `F24A`), with source_amendment_date. The header association view (fec_independent_expenditures_filing_associations) finds no filing for any row, original-filing or bulk. These native fields are valid without synthesizing generic names or choosing one date. Target expansion must not multiply the record's full amount; current/net totals need a qualified selection and financial rule. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row has the amount status `exact`.
fec_independent_expenditures.coverage: Sampled. The bulk rows are FEC's 2024-cycle independent-expenditure file (`source_cycle` 2024). The original-filing rows are the Schedule E and Form 5 lines of the filings in the daily electronic-filing archives this service retained, not a cycle: `source_cycle` is NULL on them, and `fec_collections` names each archive (join on `collection_id`). This declaration does not establish complete FEC history or current publication.
fec_independent_expenditures.data_quality:
Exact decimals preserve signs. Memo, subtotal and attribution flags require source-specific interpretation; successful mapping does not qualify current, gross or net totals. Keep reported balances, allocation totals/components, overlapping summaries and two-sided transfers at their declared grains. Quality notices do not automatically exclude records.
The bulk file is FEC's as filed, including a few single lines of billions of dollars that no committee plausibly spent: THE COMMITTEE OF 300 (C00874586) reports $9,778,412,568 in one line of its 24-hour report 1766664, exactly as its raw filing on docquery.fec.gov states it (checked 2026-10-03), not a sum of amended or memo lines. Review the largest rows before summing. On 2026-10-03 the original-filing rows came from the archives of 2026-06-08, 2026-06-09 and 2026-07-02.

legacy_column_descriptions.expenditure_date: The expenditure date the source states, distinct from dissemination date. A two-digit year (FEC's bulk file writes `25-OCT-24`) is read as the one year ending in those digits between 1975, when FEC began, and the year the file was captured (`24` is 2024; the range is `date_year_bounds` in `mapping_reason_json`). A typo that stays in the range (`26` for `24`) is typed as written and cannot be detected; `expenditure_date_raw` keeps the date as filed. NULL has its reason in `expenditure_date_status`; capture time is never substituted.
legacy_column_descriptions.dissemination_date: The dissemination date the source states, distinct from expenditure date. A two-digit year (FEC's bulk file writes `25-OCT-24`) is read as the one year ending in those digits between 1975, when FEC began, and the year the file was captured (`24` is 2024; the range is `date_year_bounds` in `mapping_reason_json`). An original filing states four digits. A typo that stays in the range (`26` for `24`) is typed as written and cannot be detected; `dissemination_date_raw` keeps the date as filed. NULL has its reason in `dissemination_date_status`; capture time is never substituted.
legacy_column_descriptions.receipt_date: The day FEC received the filing, as the source states it. A two-digit year (FEC's bulk file writes `25-OCT-24`) is read as the one year ending in those digits between 1975, when FEC began, and the year the file was captured (`25` is 2025: a 2024-cycle file holds late filings; the range is `date_year_bounds` in `mapping_reason_json`). A typo that stays in the range (`26` for `24`) is typed as written and cannot be detected; `receipt_date_raw` keeps the date as filed. NULL has its reason in `receipt_date_status`; capture time is never substituted.

fec_intercommittee_transactions.label: Reported committee-to-committee transaction observations
fec_intercommittee_transactions.summary: One reported intercommittee transaction record version. Preserves reporting committee, counterparty references, literal transaction type, memo and amount. Direction remains unresolved unless source definitions prove it; both sides of a transfer are observations until an explicit flow rule qualifies consolidation. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. Every row has the amount status `exact`.

fec_intercommittee_transactions.data_quality: Exact decimals preserve signs. Memo, subtotal and attribution flags require source-specific interpretation; successful mapping does not qualify current, gross or net totals. Keep reported balances, allocation totals/components, overlapping summaries and two-sided transfers at their declared grains. Quality notices do not automatically exclude records.

legacy_column_descriptions.source_locator_json: Exact source row or subrecord coordinates, including available member, ordinal, byte span and field-definition references. Resolve in the pinned source generation.
legacy_column_descriptions.source_namespace: Namespace identifying the native layout or identifier system. Similar numbers or field names across namespaces are not equivalent.
legacy_column_descriptions.source_record_id: Native source-observation key within collection_id. Resolve with the source generation, exact locator and source digest, not this value alone.

legacy_column_descriptions.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the original source witness bytes; distinct from the typed table's publication digest.
legacy_column_descriptions.record_id: Deterministic key for this mapped source observation within its table and generation; repeated captures remain distinct from a single economic event.

legacy_column_descriptions.filing_key: Nullable authority- and namespace-qualified filing-version key. Several retained observations can share it; group proven filing identity before joining. fec_loan_terms.label: Reported loan terms observations
fec_loan_terms.summary: One source loan-terms or credit-line record version. Preserves rate/due-date wording, collateral, security, signers and stated amounts. Loan principal, credit draw and balances are distinct concepts; this table does not infer a new disbursement for each repeated terms record. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence. Every row comes from `fec-electronic-filing-schedule`.
fec_loan_terms.coverage: Sampled. Supported observations from retained Schedule C1 loan agreement and credit-line layouts. The retained selection is explicit in fec_collections and its source-generation evidence; this declaration does not establish complete FEC history or current publication.
fec_loan_terms.data_quality: Exact decimals preserve signs. Memo, subtotal and attribution flags require source-specific interpretation; successful mapping does not qualify current, gross or net totals. Keep reported balances, allocation totals/components, overlapping summaries and two-sided transfers at their declared grains. Quality notices do not automatically exclude records.

fec_receipts.label: Campaign money received
fec_receipts.summary: One reported receipt record version or physical source observation. Preserves contributor, amount, date, transaction type, memo, source role and evidence. Main/date partitions, amendments and correction streams remain distinct observations; select proved representation membership and a named financial rule before totals. Resolve collection_id and source_record_id against fec_source_records in the captured source generation, using source_locator_json and source_sha256 to distinguish repeated witnesses. Stored or release-matched derived evidence routes preserve the same exact source coordinates. For original-filing rows, definition_set_id joins fec_filing_definitions.record_id and its fec_filing_definition_evidence context witnesses; filing_header_record_id and filing_header_locator_json identify the separate actual header witness. Other source layouts retain their own dictionary evidence.
fec_receipts.coverage: Sampled by collection, whole within one. Which FEC collections are retained is an explicit selection (fec_collections, fec_collection_selection) of individual-contribution bulk files, original-filing receipt schedules and supported receipt APIs. A retained individual-contribution bulk file is held whole, every record, so its rows here equal its fec_collections.record_count, while a retained original filing contributes only its receipt records. Cycles, filings and API scopes outside the selection are absent; this declaration does not establish complete FEC history or current publication.
fec_receipts.data_quality: Exact decimals preserve signs. Memo, subtotal and attribution flags require source-specific interpretation; successful mapping does not qualify current, gross or net totals. Keep reported balances, allocation totals/components, overlapping summaries and two-sided transfers at their declared grains. Quality notices do not automatically exclude records.

fec_reported_financial_summaries.data_quality: Two layouts repeat one figure. candidate-web-summary/1 holds a candidate's row from FEC's weball file and, for a current House or Senate campaign, an identical row from webl, a subset of weball; committee-summary-csv/1 repeats a committee's row once per linked candidate. Keep one row per layout, entity, cycle and period before summing (cycle 2026, measured 2026-10-03, with 2,949 identical candidate pairs and 70 committees repeated, every repeat identical).

org_committee_links.label: Commenter organizations matched to committees
org_committee_links.summary: One row per (commenter organization name, FEC committee) name match, derived by `build_org_committee_links`. Materializes the organization-name bridge between the regulations.gov corpus and `fec_committees` — the join the data model always described but left to each query author, so every consumer normalized names differently. `organization` is the raw string as filed, joining straight back to `comments.organization`; `committee_id` joins to `fec_committees`. Coverage is inherently small: `comments.organization` is stated on a small share of comments (`count(organization)` over `comments` is the measure) and on none at some agencies (FDA, EPA), and most commenting organizations do not run a federal PAC, so most organization names matching no committee is the expected outcome rather than a matcher to tune harder. Matching runs in three tiers (`exact`, `core`, `prefix`) and every row carries `match_method`, `confidence`, and `committee_match_count` so consumers pick their own precision bar instead of trusting an opaque score. A high `committee_match_count` can reflect multiple committees sharing a name prefix; inspect the source evidence before treating those matches as an affiliation network. The comment counts and dates on a row cover every agency and year the comments table holds and repeat on each committee row of the same organization string.
org_committee_links.coverage: Derived, and bounded by a small input. Name matches between commenter organizations and FEC committees, reachable only for the small share of comments that carry an `organization` value at all, so absence of a link is not evidence that a commenter has none. A candidate's committee or a leadership PAC is never linked.
org_committee_links.data_quality: These are heuristic name matches, not source-reported affiliations. `confidence` grades the matching rule alone, not a measured probability: it does not look at whether the committee still files or at the sponsor FEC states. Links to a candidate's committee (FEC committee type `H`, `S` or `P`) or a member's leadership PAC (designation `D`) are left out, because such a committee is never an organization's own (25 of 25 sampled were false, 2026-10-03). `connected_organization_name` and `sponsor_name_match` add FEC's own statement of each committee's sponsor beside the grade: in a seeded sample of 45 `high` links (2026-10-03, judged from FEC's committee records), 15 of 15 that agree, 13 of 15 that differ and 12 of 15 with no stated sponsor were the commenting organization's own committee or filing. Whether a committee has terminated is in `fec_committees`, one join away on `committee_id`: `filing_frequency` `T` (terminated) or `A` (administratively terminated), and `last_file_date`. A link to a terminated committee can still be right, for a comment filed while the committee was active.

columns.description: Commenter organization exactly as filed on the comment. Join key back to `comments.organization`.
Matched OpenFEC committee identifier. Joins to `fec_committees.committee_id`, whose `filing_frequency` (`T` or `A`: terminated) and `last_file_date` say whether the committee still files.
Matched committee name as registered with the FEC.
Human-readable committee type of the matched committee (e.g. `PAC - Qualified`). Never a House, Senate or presidential candidate's committee: those links are left out.
Human-readable committee designation of the matched committee. Never `Leadership PAC`: those links are left out.
Human-readable political party of the matched committee. Often null for non-party committees.
Sponsoring organization type of the matched committee (e.g. `Trade Association`, `Labor Organization`). Often null.
Two-letter state on the matched committee (`fec_committees.state`). Often null.
How the pair matched: `exact` (full normalized names equal), `core` (decoration-stripped cores equal), or `prefix` (committee core starts with the whole organization core on a token boundary).

`high` for `exact`/`core`; for `prefix`, `medium` when `committee_match_count` <= 5 and `low` above that. Grades the name match alone: it ignores whether the committee still files and the sponsor FEC states (`sponsor_name_match`). Filter on this to pick a precision bar.

How many FEC committees this organization name matched in total, counting the candidate committees and leadership PACs whose links are left out, so it can exceed this string's rows here. A high count does not establish an affiliate network; inspect source evidence alongside the matching rule.

Comments filed under this exact organization string in every agency and year the comments table holds (deduplicated on `comment_id`, newest `modify_date` wins — matching the MCP `comments` view). The same value repeats on each committee row of the string; do not sum it across rows.
Distinct dockets this organization string commented on, across every agency and year. Repeats on each committee row of the string.
Earliest `posted_date` across this organization's comments in every agency and year (ISO 8601 string).
Latest `posted_date` across this organization's comments in every agency and year (ISO 8601 string).

The committee's connected organization (its sponsor) as FEC states it, verbatim from `fec_committee_history.connected_organization_name` in the latest filing year that names one. NULL when no year names one: FEC's placeholders (`NONE`, `N/A`, `NA`, `BLANK`, `0`, punctuation alone), which that table keeps verbatim, are read as naming none. Filers sometimes write the PAC's own name, a former name or a parent company here.

Whether `connected_organization_name` names the commenting organization: `agrees` when it reduces to `organization_core` under the same normalization (read also with PAC words such as `POLITICAL ACTION COMMITTEE` removed, spaces ignored); `differs` otherwise, most often the same organization spelled another way (`ASSN`, inverted words, a typo), a former name or a parent company, sometimes a different sponsor; `not_stated` when FEC names no sponsor. A name comparison, not an identity.

Native list of the distinct agency codes this organization commented to, across every year, sorted. Repeats on each committee row of the string. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
Meaning of the stated organization-to-committee association; no shared legal identity is implied.

gao_reports.label: Government Accountability Office reports
gao_reports.summary: One GAO report or testimony, keyed by product ID. GovInfo, GAO listings/RSS, retained package data and explicit repairs supply records. The table retains earlier observations and fills missing cells; source routes have different periods and metadata. Native `/3` rows expose product URL and source route; earlier schemas retain them in receipts. Major-rule letters provide separate source-stated agency, date and RIN fields, with reading evidence in receipts.
gao_reports.coverage: True range on GovInfo's closed archive (1989-11-15–2008-09-18), combined with bounded GAO listings, recent RSS reads, retained package data and explicit repairs. Completed GAO listing scopes extend from 2009; major-rule listings reach April 1996. Recent RSS reads began 2026-09-22 and first reached 2026-09-15; the upstream copy covers 2026-07-13–2026-09-14. The retained R package reaches 1922 but adds only otherwise unheld reports. Intermediate periods remain incomplete where listing walks or repairs have not filled them. Numbered legal decisions belong to `gao_decisions`. Missing enrichment is not proof of an absent report.
gao_reports.data_quality: GovInfo metadata is read in batches; a missing report number can mean unread or unavailable MODS. Major-rule letter fields use product-page/PDF captures from 2026-10-04; later products remain blank until read. Package-supplied requester, recommendation, matters, page-count and subject fields can be missing on later reports. Product-page enrichment is implemented but disabled; its absence does not remove report records. GAO listing issue dates and Month in Review release dates differ. The retained R package (CetiAlphaFive/gao, GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230) supplements other sources and excludes legal decisions. Unnumbered products are excluded. A retained source route does not certify complete coverage of its archive.

columns.description: GAO product id as gao.gov's product URL spells it (e.g. `gao-26-107974`, `t-rced-94-121`), lowercased. Primary key / dedup key. A GovInfo package id maps to that spelling (`GAOREPORTS-GAO-HEHS-00-73` is `hehs-00-73`, `GAOREPORTS-RCED-AIMD-94-221FS` is `rcedaimd-94-221fs`); a few keep GovInfo's spelling where the package id cannot recover gao.gov's.

Product title as the route states it; on a listing row, the teaser's label and heading joined as `label: heading`, which is how the feed titles the same products. The Month in Review cuts a long heading at about 200 characters and ends it `...`; where GAO's major-rule listing states that heading whole, the title is whole. A `gao_major_rule_listing` or `gao_major_rule_index` row's is `Federal Agency Major Rule Report: ` and the heading GAO's listing or the report's product page states, or the heading alone on the AIMD- and GGD- products. A few GovInfo titles are GovInfo's placeholder `GAO Report from` and the number. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells. GAO double-escapes some headings, so a few listing titles keep `—`, `—` or `&` literally, as GAO's page displays them; apply `html.unescape` when matching.

GAO product type. The feed tags no finer type, so a feed or upstream-copied row is `Report`; a GovInfo or listing row is `Testimony` for a `T-` number or a number ending in `T`, else `Report`; NULL on a report added by explicit repair.

Publication date as an ISO date string (e.g. `2026-07-17`): the feed's `pubDate` (upstream's feed for a copied row), GovInfo's `dateIssued`, the listing's "Publicly Released" date (its "Published" date where it states no release), GAO's issue date on a `gao_major_rule_listing` or `gao_major_rule_index` row (those listings state no release date), or the day a repaired product's page states. Sort key.

The product summary: the feed's (GAO's `What GAO Found` / `Why GAO Did This Study` narrative), or a GovInfo row's MODS `abstract` with whitespace runs collapsed; NULL where neither states one, and on repair and listing rows. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells.

Reserved Native list of agencies the product covers. The RSS feed carries no structured agency tags, so this is `[]` pending a future enrichment source; NULL on repair, GovInfo (MODS names no agency) and listing rows. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

Native list of topics. A GovInfo row's is its MODS `subject/topic` terms in the record's order, GAO's own index terms, program names and places, kept as stated (a long name can arrive split in two); NULL where the MODS states none or is unread. A listing row's is GAO's own topic headings the product was listed under, as GAO spells them and in listed order; a `gao_major_rule_listing` or `gao_major_rule_index` row's is NULL, since those listings state no topic. The RSS feed carries no topic tags, so a feed or upstream-copied row is `[]`; NULL on repair rows. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

The product's page on the route that supplied the row: the gao.gov product page for feed, upstream-copied, repair and every listing's rows, GovInfo's details page (composed from the package id) for GovInfo rows.

The route that supplied the row: `gao_rss` (the daily feed), `upstream_copy` (copied once from upstream spicy-regs' published table), `gao_repair` (an explicit single-report repair), `govinfo` (GovInfo's GAOREPORTS listing), `gao_listing` (GAO's own Month in Review and Annual Index), `gao_major_rule_listing` (GAO's Congressional Review Act listing, "Reports on Major Rules"), `gao_major_rule_index` (GAO's index of 2000-12-15 of its 1996-2000 major-rule reports, and each report's product page) or `gao_r_package` (copied once from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package by Jack T. Rametta, GPL-3.0-or-later).

The publisher's product type, finer than `report_type`, which keeps its values. A GovInfo row's is its MODS type (e.g. `Letter Report`, `Correspondence`, `Testimony`, `Fact Sheet`, `Other Written Product`). A listing row has one only where GAO's teaser shows a finer type in place of a subject (`Federal Agency Major Rule Report`, on every major-rule report; `Correspondence`; `Other Written Product`); NULL where it shows a subject or only `Report`/`Testimony`. A report GAO's major-rule listings state is `Federal Agency Major Rule Report` on their word, whatever route holds its row: every `gao_major_rule_listing` and `gao_major_rule_index` row but the AIMD- and GGD- products that listing also states (NULL), and the few GovInfo rows those listings name, GAO-01-1024R among them though it reports on no rule (GAO lists it so; owner decision 2026-10-04). NULL on other routes and on unread GovInfo rows.

The report number as the route prints it, the form other documents cite and users search for: a GovInfo row's MODS (e.g. `GAO-08-919R`, `RCED/AIMD-94-221FS`, `GAO/HEHS-00-73`) or the product number on GAO's listing page (e.g. `GAO-26-108426`, `OGC-96-9` for a major-rule report of 1996 to 2000, or `B-331093` for one from April 2017 on). The listing fills it on any row it lists whose number is NULL, whatever route supplied the row, and never replaces one. NULL on other feed, upstream-copied and repair rows, and on GovInfo rows whose MODS is unread. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells.

Why GAO did the work, as the R package states it: `congressional_request`, `testimony`, `correspondence`, `cg_initiated` (the Comptroller General's own initiative) or `statutory_mandate`. NULL where the package states none, and on reports issued after its copy (2026-09-26) until a GAO product-page reader fills them.

Native list of the requesting congressional committees, as the R package extracted them from the report (e.g. `Committee on Armed Services (Senate)`). NULL where it states none, and on reports issued after its copy. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

Native list of the requesting members of Congress, as the R package extracted them from the report's text, with its OCR errors kept (e.g. `Charles H. Percy (Senate)`). NULL where it states none, and on reports issued after its copy. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

How many recommendations the product makes (0 for none): the rows of "Recommendations for Executive Action" on the report's GAO product page where a page read has set it, else the R package's count. BIGINT. NULL on reports the package does not list and no page read has reached.

How many matters for congressional consideration the product raises (0 for none): the rows of "Matter for Congressional Consideration" on the report's GAO product page where a page read has set it, else the R package's count. BIGINT. NULL on reports the package does not list and no page read has reached.
The report's page count: the pages GAO's product page states for the file it labels Full Report where a page read has set it, else the R package's. BIGINT. NULL where neither states one.

Native list of GAO's subject index terms for the product (e.g. `Cost control`, `Financial management`), finer than `topics`: the terms the report's GAO product page lists, as GAO spells them and in page order, where a page read has set it, else the R package's. GAO retags products, so the two can differ. NULL where neither states any. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

The agency that issued the rule a Federal Agency Major Rule Report is on, as the report's letter prints it in its opening sentence (e.g. `Department of Health and Human Services, Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA)`): one string in GAO's wording, abbreviations kept, the agencies of a joint rule in one clause and not split. It is not an agency key, and GAO spells one agency several ways. NULL on a row that is not a major-rule report, on one whose letter has not been read, and where the letter states no such clause.

Native list of every Regulation Identifier Number the letter of a Federal Agency Major Rule Report states for the rule or rules the report is on, each as `NNNN-LLNN` (e.g. `2040-AB75`), in the letter's order. The join key to `unified_agenda.rin` and to the entries of `federal_register.regulation_id_numbers`. The list is not paired with `major_rule_fr_citations`: entry k of one is not the RIN of entry k of the other, and a report on two rules often states one RIN for both, so take a rule's RIN beside its citation from `federal_register`. NULL on a row that is not a major-rule report or whose letter has not been read, and where the letter states none in that form: it names a docket, an FCC number or a ZRIN instead, or GAO mistyped it. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

Native list of the Federal Register citation of each rule a Federal Agency Major Rule Report is on, as its letter states it, each as `{volume}-{page}` (`66-6976` for 66 Fed. Reg. 6976), in the letter's order: one for most reports, several where a report is on several rules or on a rule published as several documents. Each joins `federal_register` on `volume` and `start_page` (`split_part(c, '-', 1) = volume AND split_part(c, '-', 2) = start_page`); a few letters cite the page before the document starts or a page inside it. A correction, a delay or an earlier rule the letter cites beside its rule is left out. Not paired with `major_rule_rins`. NULL on a row that is not a major-rule report or whose letter has not been read, and where the letter states no citation: the rule was not published in the Federal Register, or the letter's opening cites none. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
Uppercase report number, falling back to the product-page ID only when the number is NULL. Blank numbers stay blank. This is a citation lookup key; report_id remains the record identity.

crs_reports.label: Congressional Research Service reports
crs_reports.summary: One retained revision of a Congressional Research Service report's Congress.gov list metadata, keyed by `report_id` and `update_date`. Distinct dated revisions survive incremental merges; repeated copies of the same revision deduplicate. Whole or pooled list walks validate the declared population. Report details and bodies are not fetched. `MIN(published_date)` per report gives the earliest retained version's publication date, which is not necessarily its first issue. The source API locator is retained in receipts.
crs_reports.coverage: True range: reports whose current version is dated from 1993-10-22 on (`published_date` is the current version's date, not first issue).

columns.description: CRS report id (e.g. `R48641`, `IN12713`). Together with `update_date`, identifies one retained revision.
Report title as returned by the list endpoint.
CRS product category from `contentType` (e.g. `Reports`, `Posts`).
Congress.gov's own status, `Active` or `Archived`, as stated; the list route does not define it, and an `Archived` report can carry a recent `published_date`.

The publisher's `publishDate` for this retained report version, as the list route states it. Dates the version, not necessarily the first issue (R44997, first issued in 2017, carries 2026-04-29 at version 16). The list route gives no first-issue date.
Source timestamp when the Congress.gov record was updated. Together with `report_id`, identifies one retained revision; also controls the incremental fetch window.
Version number of the report as returned by the list endpoint.

court_dockets.label: Court dockets of APA suits against agencies
court_dockets.summary: One CourtListener docket object selected as nature-of-suit 899, an Administrative Procedure Act case. Search API and bulk sources cover mainly district courts; direct appellate challenges are largely absent. Agency names in case/party text identify candidates, not confirmed regulatory links. `cl_docket_id` identifies a docket object, not necessarily a unique case; use `court_docket_groups` to inspect related objects and retain reused-number ambiguity.
court_dockets.coverage: True range with a density caveat: dockets filed from 1992 on, but only the nature-of-suit 899 (Administrative Procedure Act) selection, not the full docket record. Party names of dockets from the bulk edition are read a bounded slice per run; until read, parties is NULL. Recall against the publisher's nature-of-suit coding is unmeasured.

columns.description: CourtListener docket id (e.g. `73613631`). Primary key / dedup key of a docket object, not of a case: one case can be several rows (`court_docket_groups`). Distinct from the regulations.gov `docket_id`.

Short case name (e.g. `HENNEPIN COUNTY, MINNESOTA v. U.S. DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES`). Names the defendant agency as text, not as an identifier. For decisions in cases missing here, including appeals of agency orders, search `court_opinion_clusters.case_name`.
Full case caption when available; often blank.
CourtListener court identifier (e.g. `dcd` D.D.C., `cadc` D.C. Circuit, `akd` D. Alaska).
Human-readable court name (e.g. `District Court, District of Columbia`).
Court citation abbreviation (e.g. `D.D.C.`).
Court docket number (e.g. `1:26-cv-02460`).
Date the case was filed (ISO 8601 string). Sort key and incremental watermark.
Date the case was terminated, if closed (ISO 8601 string). Null for pending cases.
Date of oral argument, if any (ISO 8601 string). Often null.

court_docket_groups.label: Court docket same-case groups
court_docket_groups.summary: One docket object's membership in an inferred same-case group. Shared court/number alone is insufficient: matching captions, or a same-day contained caption, qualify the group. `confidence_tier` separates per-defendant dockets from duplicate records. The representative is a selected display row, not a publisher-designated main case. Grouping is limited to the stated CourtListener bulk edition; reused numbers and later objects may remain ungrouped.
court_docket_groups.coverage: Not a range. A derived mapping over the published `court_dockets` selection, computed from CourtListener's bulk docket edition named in `edition`. The grouping evaluates every published row whose court and docket number hold two or more published rows and which that edition holds. Such a row has no group when the rows under its number show no sign of one case (different captions: a court reusing a number) or none has a numeric PACER case id; a row published after the edition has no group until the grouping is recomputed.

columns.description: CourtListener docket id of a grouped row in `court_dockets`. Primary key.

The group's representative row: the member with the lowest PACER case id in its court's sequence, else the lowest numeric id (see the summary). Equal to cl_docket_id on the representative's own row. Not a main case the publisher marks; it marks none.

What the group's rows are: `per_defendant_dockets` (a criminal case's per-defendant dockets: the ids the representative was chosen from run consecutively with at most four missing, or a member carries CourtListener's defendant number) or `duplicate_records` (several records of one filing). Says nothing about refiling: a refiled case gets a new docket number, which this grouping cannot see.
Number of published court_dockets rows in the same-case group.

court_docket_groups.grain: One row per grouped court_dockets row; absent rows have no group.

court_opinion_clusters.label: Court decisions and their opinion groups
court_opinion_clusters.summary: Decision metadata from CourtListener opinion-clusters bulk data and opinion-search catch-up. cluster_id joins court_opinions.cluster_id (and through it the citation map and parentheticals); cl_docket_id joins court_dockets.cl_docket_id only where both tables hold the same publisher docket object: an appellate decision can name a scraper-created docket while court_dockets holds the RECAP one, so match on the docket number when the id does not join. Court identity comes from a bulk docket map or a search result; jurisdiction classification uses CourtListener's court reference data. This table does not hold individual opinion bodies.
court_opinion_clusters.coverage: Not a range. The complete 2026-06-30 CourtListener opinion-clusters export, every mapped source field checked against the original export; the court fields agree with the same-edition docket map and court reference data. A search catch-up adds every cluster whose id is above the export's highest, whatever its filing date; a correction to an exported cluster arrives with the next export. Opinion bodies and broader historical coverage are separate. Per-court gaps are the publisher's: cadc has no unpublished cluster between 2001-04 and 2020-07. See docs/research/fork-output-ledger-2026-09-21.md and receipt join-gaps-2026-09-26/i/.
court_opinion_clusters.data_quality:
Bulk and search records expose different fields. ingest_source identifies the selected row's route; unavailable metadata may be NULL or blank. A search row never replaces a bulk row of the same export, whose ids it lies above, and a later export's bulk row replaces it. Opinion search does not index RECAP trial-court clusters, so one created after the export arrives only with the next export. Missing court scope is unknown, not proof of a non-federal court. court_dockets is a narrower selection, so unmatched docket IDs are expected. Names, judge strings and citations do not establish cross-source identity.
One decision can be several clusters. On the 2026-06-30 export (measured 2026-10-03), 131 of the 140 Supreme Court decisions reported in 600-606 U.S., grouped by `cl_docket_id` and U.S. citation, have two to five clusters, none with an `scdb_id`. That grouping is a heuristic: it cannot see a decision with no reporter citation yet.

columns.description: CourtListener opinion-cluster ID: this table's primary/dedup key, one per CourtListener record of a decision, not per decision. The publisher can hold several clusters for one decision, a Supreme Court slip opinion and its later U.S. Reports print above all, and later opinions cite either (Loper Bright: 9986254 and 10600041). Count decisions by `scdb_id`, the publisher's decision key, where it is set; it is unset on every Supreme Court cluster filed after 2019. Otherwise group by `cl_docket_id` and reporter citation (court_citations), a heuristic that misses a decision with no reporter citation yet. Join to court_opinions.cluster_id and court_citations.cluster_id; not an opinion_id.

CourtListener docket ID, renamed from docket_id. Joins court_dockets.cl_docket_id only where both tables hold the same publisher docket object (an appellate case often has two: the court-website scraper's, named here, and RECAP's, held there), so match on the docket number when the id does not join; unrelated to regulations.gov docket_id.
CourtListener court identifier from the docket map or search record; NULL when unresolved.
CourtListener jurisdiction code from the court reference lookup; NULL when unavailable.

`t` where CourtListener's jurisdiction code for the court starts with F (F appellate, FD district, FB bankruptcy, FBP bankruptcy appellate panel, FS special), `f` otherwise, as a string; NULL when the classification is unavailable. FS covers courts outside the circuit system, Article I courts and executive adjudicators among them (`cit`, `uscfc`, `cavc`, `bia`, `mspb`), so `t` does not mean an Article III court: filter `court_jurisdiction` for that.

Source Supreme Court Database minority-vote count, stored as a string.

Join cluster_id to court_opinion_clusters.cluster_id to reach the decision; a U.S. Reports citation found in a document (SpicyDocs' us_reports_cite rule) resolves through the rows with reporter 'U.S.', to every cluster carrying it (often two for a recent Supreme Court decision). Rebuilt whole from each quarterly export. All columns are VARCHAR, copied as the publisher wrote them.
court_citations.coverage: Not a range. The complete 2026-06-30 CourtListener citations export, copied field for field: every (cluster_id, volume, reporter, page) unique as the publisher's schema requires. The publisher cut this export hours after the cluster export, so a few citations name a cluster court_opinion_clusters lacks (63 on 2026-09-26, 43 of them added by the clusters' catch-up; receipt join-gaps-2026-09-26/i/).
court_citations.data_quality: Citations are the publisher's, not re-derived from opinion text; a decision missing a citation here may still carry one in print. Reporter strings are the publisher's abbreviations and are not normalized. page is text because some reporters page with letters or asterisks. A new export is refused until the published court_opinion_clusters reaches every cluster id it names; a cluster the publisher merged away after the export still dangles. court_citation_map.label: Court opinion citation map
court_citation_map.summary: Which court opinion cites which, and how often, as CourtListener's citator resolved it. Both ids are opinion ids, not decision ids: join each to court_opinions.opinion_id, then court_opinions.cluster_id to court_opinion_clusters, to ask what cites a decision or which decisions are cited most. Rebuilt whole from each quarterly export.
court_citation_map.coverage: Not a range. The complete 2026-06-30 CourtListener citation-map export: citing/cited opinion pairs, each unique as the publisher's schema requires, with no NULL depth. Only the publisher's surrogate row id is dropped. Citing and cited ids resolve through court_opinions of the same edition except a small residue (see data_quality).
court_citation_map.data_quality: On 2026-09-22 all but 3,758 citing ids and one cited id resolved through court_opinions of the same edition. The edges are the publisher's automated citation resolution, not a reviewed citator: citations it could not resolve are absent, and depth counts mentions, not treatment (followed, distinguished or overruled are not recorded). Several opinions of one decision each carry their own edges, and so do several clusters of one decision (see court_opinion_clusters.cluster_id): count decisions, not rows or clusters, by `scdb_id` where it is set, else by the heuristic `cl_docket_id` plus reporter citation, and query every cluster of a cited decision. Edges reach a recent decision late: Loper Bright (decided 2024-06-28) has one citing decision filed in 2024 against 151 for Chevron over the same months, and none of its citing clusters was created before 2025-01-13 (measured 2026-10-03 on the 2026-06-30 export); the publisher does not say why.

court_parentheticals.label: Court opinion parentheticals
court_parentheticals.summary: Short summaries of a decision written by the courts that later cite it, the text in parentheses after a citation, such as "(holding that an agency must explain a change in position)". described_opinion_id is the opinion summarized and describing_opinion_id the one that wrote it; join either to court_opinions.opinion_id to reach its decision. score is the publisher's estimate of how descriptive the text is. Rebuilt whole from each quarterly export.
court_parentheticals.coverage: Not a range. The complete 2026-06-30 CourtListener parentheticals export, none with empty text; some have no group. Described and describing opinion ids resolve through court_opinions of the same edition except a small residue (see data_quality).
court_parentheticals.data_quality: On 2026-09-22 every described opinion id and all but 618 describing ids resolved through court_opinions of the same edition. The text is the citing court's own words, extracted automatically by the publisher, so it can describe a holding, a fact or a procedural point, and score is a model estimate, not a review. Several parentheticals can summarize the same point; group_id links those the publisher grouped. The groups themselves are not available: the publisher's schema declares search_parentheticalgroup (schema-2026-06-30.sql), but no bulk listing exports it (0 of 1,076 keys on 2026-09-22), so group_id has no lookup table here.

member_vote_terms.label: Member vote terms
member_vote_terms.summary: The term each member vote counts toward (delivery decision 2). A vote on `vote_day` counts toward the term with `term_start <= vote_day < term_end`, so the day one Congress ends and the next begins belongs to the new term. Only where that finds none is an inclusive end accepted, and only if exactly one term qualifies. The term type follows the chamber (`rep`, `sen`); a term with no end date never matches. Built by `build_member_vote_terms` from `member_votes`, whose `bioguide_id` the votes rollup resolves for a Senate row (from its LIS id) and for a House row of 1990-2002 (from its printed label), and `member_terms`. Join to `member_votes` on (`vote_id`, `member_key`) and to `member_terms` on (`bioguide_id`, `term_index`).
member_vote_terms.coverage: Derived, and bounded by its inputs: one row for every `member_votes` row, matched to the member's term on the vote date.
member_vote_terms.data_quality: On 2026-09-23 all but 18 votes matched a half-open term: 15 matched only an inclusive end date and 3 matched no term, exactly as an independent replay found (fork-execution-2026-09-21/votes-qualification/complete-member-join-replay.json).

The member's key within the roll call, as in `member_votes`.
`house` or `senate`.

The member's Bioguide id, as `member_votes` carries it: stated by the Clerk for the House from 2003, and resolved at the votes merge from the LIS id for the Senate and from the Clerk's printed label for a House row of 1990-2002. NULL when the LIS id or the label resolves to no one member; a `name:` key is never read as a person.
The vote's day (YYYY-MM-DD) as the chamber printed it in Eastern time, read from `member_votes.vote_date` by the same rule as `roll_call_votes.vote_day`; NULL when the file prints no date.

`half_open` (one term with start <= day < end), `inclusive_end` (none half-open, exactly one with the end day included), `ambiguous` (more than one term either way), `unmatched` (none), `unresolved_member`, or `undated` (the file prints no date, so no term is chosen). `undated` wins over `unresolved_member`; such a row still carries `bioguide_id` wherever the member resolves.

usaspending_recipients.label: Federal award recipients
usaspending_recipients.summary: One USAspending recipient and rollup level, keyed by `recipient_id`. The public recipient API ranks trailing-12-month federal awards: daily reads refresh the top 10,000 and weekly walks select the positive-amount tail. Rows outside a selection retain prior amounts. UEI supports related SAM registrations; names are matching candidates. Parent, child and recipient levels must not be added together.
usaspending_recipients.coverage: Not a range. Weekly walks select recipients with positive trailing-12-month awards; daily reads refresh the top of the ranking. Recipients outside a run's selection keep earlier amounts, so reporting periods can differ. Observation time and source digest belong to receipts when retained; older evidence may lack them. Absence does not prove the recipient has no federal awards.

columns.description: Publisher recipient identifier including its rollup-level suffix; the table's declared record key.

Publisher-stated recipient name. Name matching identifies candidates; it does not establish organization identity.

fcc_proceedings.label: FCC proceedings
fcc_proceedings.summary: One FCC ECFS docket, keyed by its name, with native proceeding ID retained separately. Full validated creation-date walks refresh its status. Where ECFS has several documents for a name, selection prefers the original docket and then the latest edited record. Unnamed or undated records are excluded. ECFS is separate from Regulations.gov and requires an api.data.gov key. Titles are not complete topic descriptions; open dockets may have placeholder close dates.
fcc_proceedings.coverage: True range: every proceeding ECFS dates, created from 1991 on, re-read whole each run so later closings and status changes are current. A proceeding with no created date is left out, because the API's date-range queries cannot reach it.

columns.description: Proceeding (docket) number, e.g. `17-108` or `23-320`. Primary key / dedup key, and the join key to the `name` of each entry in `fcc_filings.proceedings`.

ECFS numeric identifier, reused across some docket names in retained data (301759 appears with both 17-108 and 87-432). Native filing-to-proceeding joins require name AND id_proceeding; the numeric ID alone is not globally unique. The table's primary key remains name.

Proceeding title/subject (ECFS `description_display`, falling back to `description`), e.g. `Restoring Internet Freedom`. There is no program or topic field, and titles often leave the program out: Universal Service dockets include 13-184 (`Modernizing the E-rate Program for Schools and Libraries.`) and 02-60 (`In the Matter of Rural Health Care Support Mechanism`), neither of which says universal service, and high-cost programs such as the Rural Digital Opportunity Fund (19-126) and the 5G Fund (20-32) use their own names. Search titles together with bureau_code (WC, or CC for older dockets) and known docket numbers, and find related dockets by the proceedings filings name alongside an anchor docket in fcc_filings.proceeding_names_json (for Universal Service, the umbrella docket 96-45 and 10-90). A title search gives a floor, not a complete list.
Code of the FCC bureau that owns the proceeding (e.g. `WC`).
Name of the FCC bureau that owns the proceeding (e.g. `Wireline Competition Bureau`).
ECFS `flag_rulemaking_or_docket`: `R` for rulemakings (RM- numbers), `D` for dockets.

ECFS filing-window status for the proceeding (e.g. `OPENALL`): how filings are accepted, not whether the proceeding is open. Many closed proceedings still read `OPENALL`; see date_closed for the record-level closure convention.
Timestamp the proceeding was created in ECFS (ISO 8601 string). Sort key.

ECFS-recorded closure timestamp. NULL or a future date can be used only as a record-level open convention; placeholders include 2099-12-31T23:59:59.999Z and 2100-01-31T05:00:00.000Z. Neither this convention nor a recorded closure establishes current legal effect, filing acceptance or an active comment period. Check filing_status and the specific notice's comment/reply instructions separately.
ECFS account that created the proceeding. An internal FCC username; occasionally useful for spotting bureau conventions.

ECFS `date_nprm`: date of the proceeding's Notice of Proposed Rulemaking as ECFS records it, an ISO 8601 string with the publisher's UTC offset as written (96-82: `1996-04-01T00:00:00.000-05:00`). NULL when ECFS records none; 6,023 of 21,705 dockets carry one (retained walk 2026-10-08).

ECFS `date_reporting_and_order`: date of the Report and Order as ECFS records it, an ISO 8601 string with the publisher's UTC offset as written (96-82: `1996-10-18T00:00:00.000-04:00`). NULL when ECFS records none; 5,290 of 21,705 dockets carry one (retained walk 2026-10-08).

ECFS `rule_section`: the CFR part or section the proceeding concerns, as typed by FCC staff (96-82: `PART 80 AND 87`; 96-96: `73.202(B)`). Free text, not a normalized citation. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped and a blank value is NULL (owner decision 2026-10-31): ECFS writes an empty string or a single space where it has none and pads some values (` Part 76`); the receipt's `raw_record` keeps the value as ECFS wrote it. 11,259 of 21,705 dockets carry text, 16 of them stripped (retained walk 2026-10-08).

fcc_filings.label: FCC filings
fcc_filings.summary: One FCC ECFS submission, including comments, replies, ex-parte notices and letters, keyed by `id_submission`. The public API requires an api.data.gov key. Incremental received-date windows reconcile unique filing IDs with FCC's total response header; crowded selections use reconciled submission-timestamp partitions. A first run defaults to the trailing 30 days; earlier history requires an explicit date or proceeding scope.
fcc_filings.coverage: Window. FCC ECFS filings received from 2026-08-24 onward, extended daily; earlier filings appear only in explicitly backfilled proceedings. Daily runs reread the trailing seven received-date days, so later dissemination can be missed. The newest day is partial. Proceedings reflect the last read and may retain a placeholder later reassigned by ECFS. PDF text extraction covers selected documents only; a held proceeding's count is not its ECFS total.

section_diffs.label: Bill version comparisons
section_diffs.summary: One row per compared pair of consecutive printings of one bill. `engine_name`, `engine_version` and `engine_revision` record which diff engine produced the row.
section_diffs.coverage: Sampled: consecutive printings of a bill are compared only when both bodies were acquired and parsed, from the Congresses the bill family has read.
section_diffs.data_quality: A consecutive pair that cannot be diffed — because one or both sides has no parsed tree — is a counted refusal named by table, never a row. Measured on the cold-start run of the 119th (receipt `d1-measured-run-2026-09-19/`): **3,185** refusals against 128 published comparisons, which is what a 600-printing cap over 22,064 printings implies, since a pair needs both of its sides fetched in the same run. A pair runs from a printing to its neighbour in spicy-docs' `printing_order`: publisher date, then a dateless enrolled printing by its stage (`pair_rule` `consecutive_by_date_then_stage`). A pair's neighbour can be a procedural printing (a four-section Senate engrossed amendment between the calendar printing and the enrolled bill), which the summary route refuses but this table compares, so the pair reads as nearly everything removed and then everything added. In `section_diff_items`, `financial_amounts_changed` is true on every added or removed row that carries a figure, by construction; only a modified row says a figure changed in place. Floor-amendment annotations (`(increased by $X)`) are left out of `financial_*_amounts_json` though they change the text; `financial_has_amendment_annotations` marks them. Enrolled printings carry new element ids at the publisher, so `element_id` does not join into `enr`.

amendments.coverage: Window: the 119th Congress, each amendment with its detail record (the output ledger records its qualification). Scheduled runs walk an `updateDate` window from the table's watermark, at most ninety days, and fetch detail for each amendment in it.
amendments.data_quality: The publisher's `updateDate desc` order repeats and skips amendments across page boundaries when stamps tie, so one walk can serve the declared count while missing some amendments. The builder repeats whole walks, alternating order and page size, and settles on the first of two things: a clean walk (no amendment repeated, its distinct count the declared count), which stands alone, or the walks since the count last changed pooled to exactly the declared count. A pool larger than the count is never published, but a later clean walk can still settle; a query unsettled after its walks refuses the run, as does a record without an `updateDate`. Sponsor, chamber, submitted date and the amended bill or amendment come from each amendment's detail record; the list route carries none of them. 89 House amendments name the Rules Committee as sponsor and have no member sponsor to record. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

press_releases.coverage: Window. Releases from the House and Senate Appropriations committees' feeds as captured since September 19, 2026, including items that later rotated out of a feed; bill links are inferred from release text. Not all committees, earlier history or release-page bodies. See `press-release-qualification/` and `press-link-repair/` in the fork execution receipts.
press_releases.data_quality: The bill linkage is a pattern match over the release's own words, not a publisher statement. An earlier local run falsely matched `s 2027` inside a reference to the President's 2027 budget to Senate bill 2027. The corrected matcher rejects possessive suffixes while preserving quoted bill citations; wider matching quality remains unmeasured. `matched_field` and `matched_text` carry what was matched and where: a false positive is readable from the row rather than only by re-running the matcher. One pattern is compiled per published bill in the Congresses in scope, bounded on both sides and built from the bill's own type, so a bare number matches nothing. Three states are distinct and must not be read as one: a `bill_id` with `match_rule = bill_number_in_title` or `bill_number_in_excerpt` is a match; `match_rule = unmatched` with a NULL `bill_id` means the matcher ran and found no pattern match; an all-NULL `match_rule` means no matching pass ran at all, because no `congress_bills` table was published when the rollup ran, or none was published for that release's Congress, or the release states no readable `pub_date` to scope by. The Senate feed carries no item description, so a Senate release can only ever match on its title. One consequence worth knowing before relying on these four columns: a run that cannot read `congress_bills` republishes the whole live window with NULL match columns, because this table merges row-wise and a fresh row wins whole. The next run that can read it re-derives them for every release still in the feed, so the gap normally lasts one cycle — but a release that rotates off the feed during that cycle keeps the NULL permanently. The other publisher columns are unaffected; only these four degrade.

roll_call_votes.label: House and Senate roll-call votes
roll_call_votes.summary: One row per roll call: the publisher's own tally, and the bill it refers to. The four tally columns are the publisher's own counts, NULL on a candidate election (a Speaker vote), whose choices `tallies` keeps under their own labels. A Senate count element the file leaves empty or omits (`<present/>`, `<absent/>`) is read as 0, which is what the Senate means by it (119-senate-1-15: 50 yea, 50 nay, 0 present, 0 absent).
roll_call_votes.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating. Independent Senate LIS session lists and House Clerk roll files supply votes under per-run caps. The scheduled scope is the current Congress; older Congresses require backfill. Clerk history begins in 1990, in the 101st Congress; bill-derived vote references begin in the 108th. A failed chamber listing preserves its prior rows, so chambers can lag separately. Recent votes may be reread for corrections. Bill references alone do not prove a complete session index. `vote_date` retains publisher spelling and is not a sortable date bound.
roll_call_votes.data_quality: Two statements link a roll call to a bill, and `match_rule` names the one that did. `bill_action_recorded_vote`: a `recordedVotes` entry on the bill's own action, read from `bill_vote_references`. `vote_file_legislation`: the vote file's own statement of its measure, the Clerk's `legis_num` or the Senate's document, with the file's own URL as `match_url`; on a Senate amendment vote that document is `S.Amdt.`, not a bill, so such a roll call links to a bill only where the rollup resolved one through the bill's own recorded-vote action (`count(bill_id)` over amendment votes is the measure). The bill's action wins; where two bills' actions record one roll call, the one the file names wins (the Senate passing a House bill after its Senate twin); with no recorded reference the file links alone. A procedural question, a nomination, a treaty or two different bills link nothing. Measured on the 108th and 119th (receipt `votes-backfill-2026-09-26/file-links/`), the files add 881 links and agree with the recorded reference on 1,803 of the 1,809 roll calls both link; the six others are those Senate passages. `conflict_count` is per roll call, not per run: it counts the later references, the file's included, that named a different bill for *this* roll call, and they are kept rather than dropped. Before 2003 only the file's `legis_num` links: it links 6,614 of the 7,327 files of 1990-2002 to 2,842 bills, 26 of which have no `congress_bills` row yet. A held row is relinked from its own columns without a fetch; a House row published before `legis_num` or `clerk_body_element` existed is read again once to gain both, with `vote_desc`. A Senate row published before `vote_question_text`, `vote_title`, `majority_requirement` and `modify_date` existed is read again once in the same way and gains them and any tie-breaker: until then its NULL tie-breaker columns say nothing about whether the vote was tied. The scheduled run reads the sitting Congress's such rows; an earlier Congress's are read when its number is dispatched. Replayed over the retained files of the 108th-118th, that read fills the element on all 14,503 published House rows (3,742 `committee`) and `vote_desc` on 9,191, and changes no other column and no member row; it also publishes the five votes the House vacated before recording a position, which have zero tallies, `member_vote_count` 0 and no `member_votes` rows. The Clerk's 2003 Speaker election (108-1-2), whose candidate totals contradict its members' choices, still refuses. The contract's `house_vote_legislation` rule (Congress.gov's `house-vote` listing) is no longer produced and no published row carries it: it was retired with the api.data.gov key it needed (2026-09-26). Each run fills a NULL `vote_day` on every held (completely captured) roll call from its own `vote_date` before merging, so a row published before the column existed gains it without a re-fetch. An incomplete capture is not held: it is re-fetched first each run and takes its day from the file. A linkage-only row keeps NULL.

member_votes.label: Member vote positions
member_votes.summary: One row per member's position on one roll call. `position` keeps the publisher's own word (the Clerk spells both Aye/No and Yea/Nay) and `position_normalized` carries the fold, so a count and a quotation are both answerable. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
member_votes.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating. One row per member per roll call in `roll_call_votes`, so it inherits that table's both-chambers scope, per-run cap and skip-what-is-already-held behavior exactly.
member_votes.data_quality:
House rows with `state` `XX` are the non-voting delegates and the Resident Commissioner, as the Clerk marks them. The Clerk marks them only on amendment votes and motions in committee, so leave them out when ranking voting Representatives. A member who died before a term began can appear as Not Voting on its opening quorum call, as the Clerk's file lists them. One `bioguide_id` can carry more than one spelling of `member_name`; group by `bioguide_id`. The Clerk's files of 1990-2002 (the 101st-107th Congresses) name no member by bioguide id: their rows key `name:` plus the Clerk's label (`name:Jones (NC)`), and that key identifies the row within its roll call, not a person, since at least 21 labels of those years name two different members. The `bioguide_id` on such a row is resolved at the votes merge, not stated by the Clerk (rule `house-name-crosswalk-v4`): it is the one member of that surname, state and party seated in the House in that Congress, per `members`, `member_terms` and `member_party_affiliations`, and only where the vote's day lies inside that member's term. A printed first name chooses among several members when it equals the crosswalk's, in full, in its first word or as an initial, or when it is the nickname the crosswalk's source states for the member (`Tom` for Thomas Davis), which is read once `members` publishes it. Where several still answer to the label, as a successor of the same surname does (the 105th's Capps and Bono, the 107th's Shuster), the row takes the one of them seated on the vote's day; and on a day that seats several, a label that prints no first name is the member left once those the same roll call lists under a first name are set aside (the 101st's `Smith (OR)` beside `Smith, Denny (OR)`). Anything else stays NULL, and `member_vote_terms` leaves that row `unresolved_member`. Applied to the table published 2026-10-04, the rule resolves 3,173,468 of its 3,175,523 such rows with `members` as published, and 3,175,521 with the source's nicknames: the 101st's two Smiths of Oregon and the 107th's `Davis, Tom` (2,053 rows) wait for that column. The two rows then left are one that prints the Speaker `D` (106-house-1-2) and one dated the day after its member died. Run over the rows of 2003 on with the Clerk's own ids hidden and the source's nicknames, the rule filled 6,567,134 of 6,567,152 and differed from the Clerk on two: 109-house-1-239 and -240, which state M000249 (Robert Matsui, who died before that Congress met) on the row of Doris Matsui (M001163), as Voteview records those two votes. Those rows keep the id the Clerk states. Receipt: fork-execution-2026-09-21/votes-person-crosswalk-2026-10-05/. Senate rows carry the bioguide id resolved from their LIS id through `members` at the votes merge; a Senate row still NULL has a LIS id that `members` does not hold, or holds twice (`unresolved_member`).
The Clerk lists the Speaker only on the roll calls the Speaker votes on; on the others the Speaker has no row at all, not a Not Voting row (Johnson, J000299, has no row on 54 of the 314 House roll calls of 2026, measured 2026-10-03), so an absence rate over roll calls does not apply to the Speaker. `party` is the label the publisher printed on that roll call, and a change of label starts on the roll call that first prints it: the Clerk prints Kiley (K000401) `R` through roll 95 (2026-03-18) and `I` from roll 96 (2026-03-19), while `member_party_affiliations` dates the change 2026-03-09. Use `party` for a split as the chamber recorded it, and `member_party_affiliations` for a party as of a date.

The file-stated id: `lis:` plus the LIS id on a Senate record, the bare bioguide id on a House one, and `name:` plus the publisher's name where the file states neither (every Clerk file of 1990-2002). A Senate bioguide comes from the crosswalk and does not always resolve, so keying on it would split one member's votes across two rows; an identity column also cannot be null, which the design's bioguide key would have been. A `name:` key identifies the row within its roll call, not a person: across 1990-2002 at least 21 of the Clerk's labels name two different members (Jones (NC), Allen, Schiff, Wilson, McHugh, Smith (WA)...), so a person is the host's crosswalk, never this key. Congress, member_name, party and state do not identify one either: one Congress can seat a successor of the same surname, party and state (where the Clerk states bioguide ids, 5 such keys name two: 109th Matsui D-CA, 110th Carson D-IN, 112th Payne D-NJ, 117th Letlow R-LA, 119th Grijalva D-AZ; in 1990-2002 the 105th's Capps and Bono (CA) and the 107th's Shuster (PA) show it as a gap inside the Congress), so the crosswalk adds vote_date, checked against each member's service dates.

The voting member's bioguide id: stated by the publisher on a House row (the Clerk's name-id, from 2003), and filled by the host's crosswalk at merge time on a Senate row, whose file states only lis_id (members.lis_id resolves it); NULL where neither supplies one.
The voting member's Senate LIS id, which only the Senate file carries.
The member's name exactly as the roll-call source spells it.
The member's party as the roll-call source states it.

The member's state as the roll-call source states it. On a House row `XX` is the Clerk's marking for the non-voting delegates and the Resident Commissioner, on the roll calls they voted in: 2,169 of the Clerk's 22,512 of 1990-2026 (1993-1994, 2007-2010, 2019-2020 and from 2022; none in 2021), every one an amendment vote or a motion in committee (to rise, to strike or limit debate, a call in committee, a ruling of the chair), filed under <committee> (clerk_body_element on roll_call_votes) from 2007 and under <chamber> in 1993-1994.  Kept as stated, not mapped to a territory.

That position folded onto yea, nay, present or not_voting; NULL for a named candidate choice.
The chamber's literal date; sorts as text, not by time (see roll_call_votes `vote_day`).

committee_reports.label: Committee reports
committee_reports.summary: One row per published part of a captured GovInfo committee report package, keyed `(package_id, part_id)`. `bill_id` is the measure the report accompanies, read from the package's own MODS metadata.
committee_reports.coverage: Sampled. Selected committee report packages from GovInfo, a mixed-Congress selection that grows as packages are added; not complete historical or constituent-granule coverage. committee_report_reads records each package read and its outcome.
committee_reports.data_quality: Only the MODS PRIMARY bill fills bill_id. The CBO columns come from spicy-docs read_cbo_estimate on the same body already acquired. The cover recital gates publication of a letter: a CBO heading alone is not an estimate. report_states_estimate=false records an absent recital; NULL means the rule has not run. cbo_letter_count counts the letters located in the part, each a committee_report_cbo_letters row; a positive recital with a count of 0 is a declared estimate no letter was located for, distinct from an extracted letter. The five per-letter columns this table carried until committee_reports legislative-documents/2 (the first letter's span, digest, end rule and signatory) are on committee_report_cbo_letters, one row per letter (ss-uep5). estimate_heading stays here with a two-sided meaning: the part's first estimate heading where no located letter opens on it, NULL where one does (that letter's row carries it). It keeps all 115 headings of live generation 670476640e83 that open no letter, among them 110 undeclared reports' "Congressional Budget Office Cost Estimate" sections saying none was received; the other 29 live headings opened a letter and are on its row. recital_bill_id comes from the printed recital and is retained beside the MODS bill_id. bill_id is the part's own PRIMARY bill: a multi-part package's root states none, so each part of CRPT-119hrpt494 carries the H.R. 3495 its constituent record names, where its row read before parts were keyed has NULL; its separate recital_bill_id is a text interpretation. Every part a record states is read, all or none: a package whose parts cannot all be read is refused in committee_report_reads and keeps its prior rows. Parts, by decision 29 (`docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`): a report published in one part is one row whose part_id is its package id and whose part_number is NULL; a report published as parts is one row per part, part_id the part's granule id (CRPT-119hrpt455-pt2) and part_number 1 to N, except that a Part 1 the publisher left unsuffixed (CRPT-119hrpt494) has part_id equal to the package id and part_number 1. A package whose one part is spelled -pt1 (CRPT-119hrpt811; spicy-docs `docs/tables.md` names the others it measured) is (package-pt1, 1), the same shape as Part 1 of two, so a reader counts a package's rows to tell a lone part from Part 1 of several. title, date_issued and last_modified are the package's and repeat on every part row. A row published before part_id existed is kept as its package's one part (part_id the package id, part_number NULL) until the package is read again, which replaces its rows as a set; the committee_report_reads rule version re-reads every report once for this, which is what re-keys the CRPT-119hrpt811 row published 2026-09-24 as (CRPT-119hrpt811-pt1, 1).
